Moses agreed to pray that God would lift the fourth plague, and in faith he set the time of its removal, which was the next day, but he warned Pharaoh against going back on his promise, because that is falsehood and deceit that exposes him to God's punishment.
Do not take lightly lying or any sin, because it is directed against God Himself, and the wages of sin is death.

entries.section: (3) The plague of flies (the fourth plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses prayed, and God removed the plague completely from all the land of Egypt.

entries.section: (3) The plague of flies (the fourth plague)

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh returned to the hardness of his heart, went back on his promise and refused to let the children of Israel go. The plagues of the murrain of cattle, the boils, and the hail and fire.

entries.section: (1) The plague of the murrain of cattle (the fifth plague)

paragraphs.text: God commanded Moses to repeat the demand to Pharaoh to let his people go, otherwise He would strike all the cattle of Egypt with murrain and they would die.

Some cattle, such as the bull Apis, were sacred and were worshipped by the Egyptians, since the god Osiris was thought to dwell in it, so the death of the cattle shows the weakness of the god Osiris, who is one of the most important of the Egyptian gods. In this plague a divine retribution appears, which is:
1- His protection of the cattle of His people and the death of the cattle of the wicked and stubborn, that is, the Egyptians.
2- The overthrow of the pagan worship that worships animals, such as the bull Apis.
3- The power of God is shown, in which He sets the time and the place, striking the cattle in the field and on the mountain, that is, everywhere the Egyptians own cattle, and the time is tomorrow.

4- God's shattering of the pride of the great and also the strength of the army that uses horses, by their death. The death of the cattle signifies the death of the animal lusts within man, that is, God helps them to leave their lusts so that they may believe in Him.

Here God's longsuffering toward the stubborn and the rejecting is shown, that perhaps they might repent, so He repeats His demand that His people be let go and repeats the plagues, that perhaps they might fear Him and repent.

entries.section: (1) The plague of the murrain of cattle (the fifth plague)

paragraphs.text: God's protection and blessing of His children is shown in the fact that the cattle of the children of Israel did not die.

Trust in God's blessing upon you, however much those around you persecute you and trouble you, for He compensates you by blessing what you have and keeping it, and He also grants you peace and joy because you feel that God is with you.

entries.section: (1) The plague of the murrain of cattle (the fifth plague)

paragraphs.text: God showed His power in setting the time of the plague, so that no one could say that it was due to anything other than God. All the cattle that belonged to the Egyptians died, but of those that belonged to the children of Israel not one died.

entries.section: (1) The plague of the murrain of cattle (the fifth plague)

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh was alarmed by the death of all his cattle and sent messengers to the land of Goshen to learn what had happened to the numerous cattle of the children of Israel, since they worked as shepherds, and he found all their cattle unharmed. Instead of believing, he became enraged and hardened his heart and refused to let the children of Israel go to worship God.
When you see God's blessing with others, look for their virtues and the grace that is with them, so that you may follow their example instead of envying them or being jealous of them.

entries.section: (2) The plague of boils (the sixth plague)

paragraphs.text: This is the sixth plague, in which God commanded Moses to take ashes of the furnace (the oven or the altar on which sacrifices are burned) and throw them into the air, so that they became boils breaking forth with sores, that is, pus, on all the Egyptians, whether the king, the people or the priests, and even the magicians (v. 11). It is painful, and in addition it defiles the priests, who care about their purity when they approach the gods, and it gives an ugly appearance and troublesome signs of disease.

In their worship the Egyptians used to offer human sacrifices to their gods, burning them and scattering their ashes, believing that every particle of ash was a blessing from the gods. In this plague Moses showed them the futility of their worship, since this ash became painful boils on their bodies.
This plague of boils signifies the sins that disfigure man before God and pain his heart, so that he loses his peace.

entries.section: (2) The plague of boils (the sixth plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses sprinkled the ashes, and they became boils on the Egyptians and their beasts.

One wonders, where did the Egyptians get beasts after the previous plague (the murrain of cattle)? They may have bought cattle from the children of Israel after their own cattle died, or they may have bought them from the surrounding countries such as Sudan and Libya.
The boils also appeared on the diviners and magicians who assisted Pharaoh, so the weakness of Pharaoh and his helpers was revealed.

It is noticeable that Moses sprinkled the ashes toward heaven to announce that this plague was a heavenly punishment for them, that is, from God and not from their pagan gods. This plague was later called the botch of Egypt, as in (Deut 28:27), and God used to threaten the pagan peoples with it.

entries.section: (2) The plague of boils (the sixth plague)

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh persisted in his stubbornness and hardness of heart, although this was the sixth plague, and the power of his gods had been shattered before him and his weakness and that of all his helpers had been shown.
Would that you would benefit from your weaknesses and repent before the opportunity is lost, for stubbornness shows your ignorance and deprives you of God's mercies.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: God sent a rebuke to Pharaoh with Moses for his stubbornness in not letting His people go, and declared to him that He was able to kill him and all his people, but that He kept him in order to give him an opportunity to repent and to show His wonders through his hardness.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: He threatened him that He would rain hail, that is, sharp balls or sheets of ice, descending in great quantities from heaven, striking and killing everyone they meet. This plague is very great, so God warned him of it that perhaps he might repent, and kept it near the end because of its severity; it is the seventh plague, which shows the divine wrath against the stubborn and unbelieving, and in it the power of God is shown by setting the time of the plague by the day and the hour, in His saying, "To morrow about this time."

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: God warned Pharaoh and the Egyptians to take shelter in the houses and not to stand in the fields or open places, lest they and their cattle die. Some were afraid and took shelter, but whoever did not believe and remained outside his house died in this plague. Here the mercy of the One who does not desire the destruction of the Egyptians, but their faith and repentance, is shown.

God's commandments are warnings to you, that you may repent before the day of judgment comes; likewise the guidance of your father of confession and all the teachings of the Church try to rescue you, so seize these opportunities to repent and set your way right, and even to establish a relationship with God so that you may enjoy His love.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses stretched out his hand, and the violent seventh plague began, consisting of three parts that combined together to destroy the wicked:
1- Thunders: disturbing sounds that represent the warnings of God.
2- Hail: sharp ice, which signifies the divine wrath from heaven.

3- Fire: it burns whoever meets it, and it signifies our just God, who is a consuming fire. The wonder appears here, which is the union of fire with ice in one plague, because ice needs cold in order to form and fire is a heat suited to the hot climate and melts everything that is frozen.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: This plague had never happened before in Egypt, because it is distinguished by a mild climate in which thunder and hail are rare, while fire is utterly foreign to its weather conditions.

God allows adverse and strange circumstances in your life that perhaps may lead you to repentance, so when you lose some of your possessions or your dignity, know that God is calling you to return to Him.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: The hail struck all the stubborn who did not enter their houses, they and their cattle, and they died, and it also ruined and destroyed the plants and trees.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: Here too God's distinguishing of His people is shown, for this plague did not come upon them like the rest of the plagues.
Your faith in God protects you from many troubles, so do not be disturbed by God's punishment of the wicked, because you are safe within His hand.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: Stay any longer: continue to dwell in Egypt.

Pharaoh was alarmed by this plague more than by all the previous plagues, and for the first time he declared that he was a sinner and that God was righteous, and he humbly begged Moses to take this plague away from him, and promised to let the people go to worship God.
Do not rush into promises and vows during your distress because of your need, and then retreat from them when the crisis is relieved.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses agreed to pray for the plague to be lifted, but by God's guidance, as a prophet who knew of the hardness of Pharaoh's heart and that he was a liar and deceiver in his promises and would not let the people go.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: In the ear: bearing ears.
Bolled: ripened and formed seeds.
Wheat: the grain, that is, wheat.
Rie: legumes such as beans and lentils.

The plague of hail came in the spring, when the barley and the flax were ripe, and this plague destroyed them, while the wheat and the legumes were only small plants, so they were not harmed and their crop was not ruined.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: When Moses prayed, the plague ceased and the rain, the hail and the fire stopped.

entries.section: (3) The plague of hail and fire (the seventh plague)

paragraphs.text: After the plague ceased, Pharaoh returned to the hardness of his heart and refused to let God's people go. The plagues of the locusts and the darkness.

entries.section: (1) The threat of the plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

paragraphs.text: The Lord asked Moses to go in to Pharaoh and ask him to let His people go, but he would refuse, so that God might be glorified in the hardness of his heart, and it would be a lesson for all generations and a strengthening of the faith of God's people throughout the days, so that fathers would teach their children how great is God's power, His protection of His children and His punishment of their enemies.
Take care to teach your children faith in God and the Church, so that they may have the spiritual sense and feel God's work in the events around them and live reassured in His care.

entries.section: (1) The threat of the plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses and Aaron rebuked Pharaoh for not letting God's people go, that he might turn back from the hardness of his heart.

entries.section: (1) The threat of the plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

paragraphs.text: Moses also threatened him that if he did not let the people of the children of Israel go, God would strike him with the eighth plague, which is the plague of locusts, which would come in enormous numbers, not only as locusts usually do but in many times the usual swarms, for Egypt had never seen an attack of locusts like it, and it would eat every green thing in Egypt, whether small plants or trees, and would cover not only the fields but also the houses. The "residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth" means the wheat, the rie, the fruit of the trees in which something may have survived, and the grain kept in the open storehouses. Then Moses and Aaron went out of the palace and left him to the hardness of his heart and his distress at the divine threat. This shows the weakness of the Egyptian gods, unable to protect the Egyptians from the locusts that eat their necessary food, for Egypt is an agricultural country, and if its plants were spoiled, it would fall into great hunger.

The men of the royal court and Pharaoh's counselors felt the power of the God of the Hebrews, who had ruined Egypt and shown the helplessness of its gods, and they were finally forced to reproach Pharaoh and demand that he let the children of Israel go. Although their opposing Pharaoh could cost them their lives, their severe distress and frustration drove them to it.

Pharaoh was moved by his servants' words and was convinced of their truth, for he felt the power of God, so he agreed to the idea of the people going out to worship God. But the hardness of his heart made him refuse to let all the children of Israel go, and he wanted to specify certain classes of them to go out, and in this it appears that his obedience to God was incomplete. We notice that Pharaoh had agreed that they should sacrifice to God in the land of Egypt (ch. 8:25) and Moses refused that; then he agreed again to the children of Israel going out to sacrifice to God, but at a short distance from Egypt (ch. 8:28), and Moses refused that too, insisting on carrying out God's word in full. Here he agreed to their going a three days' journey, but on condition that not all the children of Israel go out.
Moses insisted that they all go, young and old, men and women, that is, all the people with their cattle, to worship God and keep a feast to Him.

Because of the severity of the plagues that had fallen on Pharaoh and the Egyptians, he tried to trick Moses, pretending to pity the children of Israel, and said that only the men should go and should not take women or children with them, lest they be exposed to the hardships of travel in the desert, such as hunger, thirst and wild animals, "evil is before you." Moses rejected his proposal, and here Pharaoh became angry and drove them out from his presence, for he signaled to his servants and they put them out from before him with contempt.

Do not negotiate with the devil over any sin, for he is evil and may begin by making you fall into laxity over a small sin or negligence in one of the spiritual practices, planning a greater evil for you with time. Persevere in your striving and increase your clinging to God, and the devil will be crushed under your feet.

entries.section: (3) The plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

paragraphs.text: The Lord commanded Moses to stretch out his rod and command the plague of locusts to eat every green plant remaining in Egypt, after the plague of hail had destroyed most of the plants.

entries.section: (3) The plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

paragraphs.text: An east wind carried enormous swarms of locusts over all the land of Egypt, and they ate everything green in it, and because of the multitude of locusts flying in the air, they hid the light of the sun so that it was like dark night.
Distance from God robs man of his strength and his material comfort, that perhaps he may return and repent and so find the salvation of his soul.

entries.section: (4) The removal of the plague of locusts

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh felt his helplessness and the ruin of Egypt and its exposure to hunger and certain death, so he summoned Moses and Aaron and declared his fault before them and begged them to remove the locusts from him, and promised to let the people go, and that this would be the last plague they would remove from him.
Do not trust the promises of the devil or of the wicked who are his helpers, for he is a deceiver; hold fast to God alone and His commandments.

entries.section: (4) The removal of the plague of locusts

paragraphs.text: Moses prayed to God, and He sent a west wind, the opposite of the east wind that had carried the locusts to Egypt, and it was stronger than the east wind, so it carried all the locusts out of Egypt and cast them into the Red Sea (the Sea of Reeds), and Egypt was rid of the locusts.
God is able to do all things, so do not fear harsh circumstances, however difficult they seem, for God has many ways to resolve them.

entries.section: (4) The removal of the plague of locusts

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh returned to the hardness of his heart and refused to let the people go.

entries.section: (5) The plague of darkness (the ninth plague)

paragraphs.text: God commanded Moses to stretch out his hand and command the ninth plague, which is the plague of darkness over all the land of Egypt. It is noticeable here that Moses did not threaten Pharaoh before this plague of darkness because of the hardness of his heart and his unreadiness to hear the voice of God. The sun was hidden and there was complete darkness over all the land of Egypt, a thick darkness with no light of moon or stars, and its intensity is expressed by saying that it could almost be felt, as if the darkness were a wall that a person could touch. This plague showed the helplessness of their great god Ra, that is, the sun, which they worshipped. Of course there was great fear in all the land of Egypt, which the Book of Wisdom describes in detail, speaking of the movement of insects and animals in the darkness and the terror that left the Egyptians almost dead.

entries.section: (5) The plague of darkness (the ninth plague)

paragraphs.text: The darkness lasted three days, during which no Egyptian moved from his place because of his fear, and none saw another; but on the other side there was light in the land of Goshen, and this plague did not come upon them as the other plagues did not.
This plague signifies the spiritual blindness that afflicts those far from God, while His children enjoy His shining upon them and their ability to discern.
If God has revealed Himself to you, hold fast to His commandments and seize the opportunity of your nearness to Him, so that you may enjoy more of His light and be delivered from the darkness of sin.

entries.section: (6) The removal of the plague of darkness

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh returned to negotiate with Moses to let all the people go, men, women and children, but on condition that they not take their flocks with them, for he did not want complete obedience to God because of the hardness of his heart.

Do not obey some of the commandments and leave out one commandment, or God's wrath will come upon you. And do not let the devil reign over any of your senses or any of your abilities, however small, and do not be lenient about seeing or possessing anything that can make you fall into sin, because the devil will not rest and will fight you with it to make you fall; so cut off from yourself everything that defiles you, and hold fast to your purity and all God's commandments.

entries.section: (6) The removal of the plague of darkness

paragraphs.text: Hoof: the singular of hooves, which is the front of the animal's foot, resembling a nail.

"Wherewith we must serve the Lord": that is, we cannot worship the Lord without offering sacrifices from the cattle, and we do not know the number of animals we shall sacrifice, so we must take all our cattle.
Moses refused, and also asked that they take their cattle with them so that they might be able to offer sacrifices to God.

entries.section: (6) The removal of the plague of darkness

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh became angry and hardened his heart and refused to obey the word of God; indeed, in his anger he told Moses and Aaron that he did not want to see them again and that they should disappear from before him forever, that is, he refused to meet them forever.
Persisting in sin makes man shut before himself the opportunities of repentance until the end, and so he loses the salvation of his soul.

entries.section: (6) The removal of the plague of darkness

paragraphs.text: Moses agreed to Pharaoh's word that he would not see him again. In Pharaoh's mind was anger against Moses, while in Moses' mind was that Pharaoh would die. This indeed happened when he was drowned in the Red Sea.
The announcement of the plague of the firstborn

entries.section: (1) The tenth plague and the spoiling of the Egyptians

paragraphs.text: After the plague of darkness, God spoke to Moses and reassured him that the coming plague would be the last and would be so severe that Pharaoh would send them out of Egypt quickly and drive them out in his great fear of their God. The Lord said this to Moses to strengthen him, so that he would not be disturbed by Pharaoh's coming threats, or those mentioned at the end of the previous chapter, that he would kill him if he saw him again.

entries.section: (1) The tenth plague and the spoiling of the Egyptians

paragraphs.text: The Egyptians had humiliated the children of Israel and robbed them of their wages by forcing them into building works, so God wanted to return to them something of their material rights from the Egyptians, and He commanded them to borrow from their Egyptian friends jewels of gold and silver. This is not theft, because it was God who commanded it, and it is the carrying out of His commandments, in order to discipline the Egyptians for their greed, covetousness and exploitation of His people.
Do not be unjust and harsh toward others, because the just God sees you and will requite you at the proper time; indeed, He may strengthen the weak person you wronged against you.

entries.section: (1) The tenth plague and the spoiling of the Egyptians

paragraphs.text: God gave His people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that on the one hand they loved them, and on the other hand they feared them and their God. So when they asked them for gold, they gave it to them immediately, although they knew that they were departing from Egypt; that is, they tried to appease them in every way, so they gave them whatever they wanted of gold and silver. As for Moses, Pharaoh's servants and the great men of the state feared him.

Some doubt that the writer of the book is the prophet Moses, since it says here "the man Moses" and does not say "I"; but the truth is that he speaks with humility, saying "the man," and then declares the greatness of God's work with him.

entries.section: (2) The threat of the plague of the firstborn

paragraphs.text: When Pharaoh called Moses and discussed with him leaving Egypt but without the cattle, Moses rejected this proposal and spoke to him with strength and firmness, and declared to him, as the Lord had commanded him, the tenth plague, the plague of the firstborn, in which God goes out in the form of an angel at midnight and kills every firstborn in all the houses of the Egyptians, whether the firstborn of the king or the firstborn of the manservant and the maidservant, and also the firstborn of the beasts.

The firstborn of the Egyptians signifies the firstborn of evil, that is, the greatest and most dreadful evil in you, and midnight signifies the darkness in which sin spreads. Cut off the head of sin and its source so that you may rest from it, for there is no truce with the devil.

entries.section: (2) The threat of the plague of the firstborn

paragraphs.text: This plague would be terrifying and beyond the Egyptians' endurance, and would be universal in all the houses, so there would be a great cry in all the houses of the Egyptians.
If God allows you a tribulation, do not be content with crying out from its pain, but return to God with repentance, and He will forgive you and heal you of its pains.

entries.section: (2) The threat of the plague of the firstborn

paragraphs.text: "Shall not a dog move his tongue": no one will harm them.
Moses also declared that God would distinguish His people, so that no harm would touch them or their beasts, but they would be in peace, despite the great suffering of the Egyptians.

entries.section: (2) The threat of the plague of the firstborn

paragraphs.text: "Great anger": intense anger, which is a holy anger here because it declares the power of God.

Moses also declared to Pharaoh that his servants would come to him and beg him and bow down before him, that perhaps he would be willing to go out from Egypt, he and the children of Israel. That is, Pharaoh would agree and submit and seek Moses' favor out of the great fear in him. The bowing down of his servants means their fear of Moses and not worship of him.

After Moses threatened Pharaoh with firm and strong words, Pharaoh became angry and said to him, as was mentioned at the end of (ch. 10), do not appear before me again or I will kill you, and Moses agreed and told him that indeed he would not see him again, because he knew that he would die. Then he went out from Pharaoh in anger and strength.

God warned Moses of Pharaoh's stubbornness and informed him that he would refuse his word, and He permits this so that He may be glorified and His power may be shown above all the gods of the Egyptians.

Do not be disturbed by the arrogance of the wicked and their power, for God is longsuffering toward them and then disciplines them, and know that they resist the good in you because they are wicked... so stand firm in your faith that you may receive the eternal reward.
This is a summary of Pharaoh's reactions to all the plagues, which is that he was still stubborn and did not want to submit to God.
The Passover and the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt after the plague of the firstborn

The beginning of months: the month of Abib was the seventh in the civil year, and after the Babylonian captivity they also called it Nisan, and God made it the first of the months of the religious year because the slaughter of the Passover lamb takes place at its beginning and the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt took place in it. Thus the Jews came to have a civil year in which the month of Abib is the seventh, and a religious year in which the month of Abib is the first, that is, the difference between the two years is six months. The word Abib means the green ear of grain, because this month comes in the spring; the Copts took the same name and put it in their months, but at another time, which is the summer.

After Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh's palace for the last time, God declared to them the most important law in the Old Testament, which is the feast of the Passover, because it is the pivot of the Old Testament, since it clearly signifies the redemption of Christ. So He appointed for them that the month in which they were, the month of Abib, would be the beginning of months and the first of them, meaning that redemption is the foundation of the faith and the beginning of everything, whose results we receive in the New Testament through the Holy Sacraments.
"According to the house of their fathers": that is, according to the number of families or households in each tribe.
"According to the number of the souls": the number of the members of the household.
"Every man according to his eating": that is, the amount of food for adults is more than for children.

The law is summed up in that every house takes a lamb to slaughter for itself and eat of it, and the size of the lamb is according to the number of members of the household, that is, Christ satisfies the whole household, large or small. If the household is small, it takes its neighbor with it and the two slaughter one lamb. This neighbor signifies the Gentiles, that is, the people of God proclaim Christ so that the whole world may believe.
The time for taking the lamb is the tenth day, and this signifies that after the Ten Commandments in the Old Testament comes Christ the Redeemer.
God requires of the lamb that is to be slaughtered the following:
"Without blemish": because Christ is a lamb without blemish, that is, without sin.
"A male": because Christ is male, that is, a bridegroom to the soul.
"Of the first year": that is, full of vitality and youth, as Christ is the source of life.
"From the sheep, or from the goats": the sheep or the goat is distinguished by obedience and gentleness, so it signifies Christ, who was obedient unto death and was in constant peace.
From this it appears that the Passover lamb is a clear type of the crucified Christ. And the choosing of the lamb as a male is not only because it signifies Christ but also:
1- Because it redeems the males of the children of Israel, who were dying from the severity of the labor or were being killed by Pharaoh by being cast into the river (ch. 1).
2- Because it redeems the male firstborn of the children of Israel at the time when the angel kills the firstborn of Egypt.

It is kept until the fourteenth day to make sure of its soundness so that God is not offered anything defective, and the fourteenth day is when the moon is full. The moon signifies the Church, for Christ is the Redeemer of the Church in the perfection of her splendor and brightness. And its remaining four days has other spiritual and psychological meanings, in addition to making sure of its soundness, and these meanings are:
1- The family's feeling that the lamb has become like one of its members, just as Christ lived among the Jews as one of them and then redeemed them and redeemed humanity.
2- Its remaining four days signifies their bondage of 400 years in Egypt.
3- That they might contemplate and think about their salvation, which would be accomplished by the slaughter of the lamb, which signifies Christ.

"In the evening": this is what the Jews call the first evening, that is, sunset, when the sun inclines toward the west at the ninth hour, which is three o'clock in the afternoon by present reckoning. The second evening is the disappearance of the sun with all its traces, that is, the red twilight, and this is at the eleventh hour, which is five o'clock in the evening by present reckoning. So the lamb is slaughtered between the two evenings, that is, from the ninth hour to the eleventh, and the Lord Christ died on the Cross at the ninth hour, that is, after the first evening, at the same time as the slaughter of the Passover lamb.
After the slaughter of the lamb they take of its blood and strike it on:
The two side posts: that is, the sides of the door, right and left, which signifies the Old and New Testaments and also signifies the Jews and the Gentiles, for Christ is the Savior of all.

The upper door post: that is, the top of the door, which signifies man's thought and head, that is, the most important part of him; and he did not strike the lower threshold, lest people tread on it when entering the house.
"Roast": a symbol of the sufferings of Christ, and they usually roasted it on two skewers crossing each other, that is, in the form of a cross, as a symbol of the crucifixion of Christ.
Roasting is also the quickest way to cook meat, so it reminds them of their haste when leaving Egypt.

"Unleavened bread": that is, without leaven, because leaven signifies evil and unleavened bread signifies purity, that is, they eat it with a pure heart; and because they were in haste to leave Egypt, their dough did not ferment, so they ate it unleavened after eating the Passover. "Bitter herbs": they signify the bitterness of sin, which is removed by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, that is, the slaughtered, roasted lamb; the bitterness signifies repentance for the sins that embittered the soul, in addition to indicating the bitterness of the bondage they suffered in Egypt.

"Raw, nor sodden": this signifies spiritual softness, sloth and laxity, in addition to the fact that raw meat comes with its blood, which the law later forbade, and which was a custom before the law, so that they would not share with the pagans who eat meat with its blood.

"His head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof": that is, we take the whole of Christ within us and do not neglect any of His commandments, even if it seems small like the feet, that is, the legs. And we take the depths of the commandment, that is, the inward parts of the lamb.

Because of its holiness and importance it is eaten entire and nothing of it is left, so that it is not exposed to corruption or mixing with any foods. And its burning is to confirm the death of Christ for us and to keep the meat from corruption. Therefore in the New Testament the Church leaves nothing of Christ's sacrifice on the altar after the Liturgy, that is, His Body and Blood. And its being eaten in one night with none of it left until morning reminds them of their eating the Passover and their leaving Egypt in one night and their deliverance from bondage.

It is also required in the manner of eating it that they eat it ready to depart, because they would leave Egypt after a few hours, since the angel would strike the firstborn and the Egyptians would ask them to hurry out of Egypt. Readiness to depart is expressed by the following:

"With your loins girded": that is, they tie their waists with a leather belt as a sign of readiness for travel or work and striving. These are the characteristics of the one who strives spiritually, that is, no self-indulgence and readiness to labor with energy in worship and service.

"Your shoes on your feet": shoes signify protection from the thorns of the ground, which signify the thorns of sin. St. Paul the Apostle tells us that shoes are the preparation of the gospel of peace, that is, carrying out the commandments. "Your staff": the staff signifies the power of God and the Cross and the rod of Moses, that is, that they rely on the power of God. "In haste": quickly, because this shows their attention to it, and because Pharaoh would hurry them to leave Egypt out of his fear after the plague of the firstborn (v. 31). It signifies spiritual wakefulness and attention to spiritual striving, and not putting off Communion because of the busyness of life. "Passover": its meaning is passing over, and in Coptic it is Pascha, a memorial of the destroying angel passing over their houses and killing the firstborn of Egypt; it is the cause of their salvation, for by the blood of the Passover lamb they received salvation.

"I will pass through the land of Egypt": the power of God, represented by the destroying angel, passes through all Egypt. The tenth plague, with the other plagues, shows the power of God above all the power of the pagan gods, and it subdues Pharaoh, who was a god, because the firstborn of all, among them Pharaoh's firstborn, will die.

It clearly confirms that the protection of the firstborn of His people is by the blood struck on the doors, and it signifies the blood of Christ, which protects us from the devil's wars and which we receive through the Holy Sacraments. So when the angel passes over he sees the blood and does not kill anyone in that house, because of their faith and their obedience to God in slaughtering the lamb and striking the door with the blood.

God asked Moses that they not make this Passover once only, but that the feast of the Passover be kept every year, so that they might prepare for the Christ who was coming to redeem them, whom the Passover lamb signifies, and that they continue to keep the Passover throughout their generations until Christ our new Passover comes and redeems us on the Cross.
Take care to prepare for partaking of the Holy Sacraments so that they may work in you with power, however difficult the circumstances around you.

Leaven signifies evil, so God asked the children of Israel, after keeping the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day, to eat unleavened bread as a sign of purity, and to go on eating it for seven days from the fifteenth day (from the evening of the fourteenth day) until the twenty-first day.
"That soul shall be cut off from Israel": set apart and removed from the congregation of the children of Israel.
"An holy convocation": that is, this day is set apart for the worship of God and works of goodness.

God also adds the keeping of two feasts of unleavened bread, on the first day, which is the fifteenth, and on the last day, which is the twenty-first, in this feast. They come to the tabernacle of the congregation and offer prayers, and a sermon may be added. They eat unleavened bread to show the purity of their hearts, and they free themselves for the feast every year and leave their daily work, doing no material work except the preparing of food.
The feasts of the Jews are seven, as mentioned in (Lev 23).
Take care to purify the heart by repentance, especially at feasts and spiritual occasions, so that you may be free for the worship of God and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him.
"In this selfsame day": that is, the fifteenth day of Nisan.

"I brought your armies out": He called them His armies because they are His people, obedient to His commands like soldiers. And He said "I brought out" although they had not yet gone out, because He, exalted is He, had decreed it, so it is certain that He will accomplish it.

God required them to continue this law throughout their lives and the lives of their children, for these feasts help toward pure conduct before God, which results from the slaughter of the lamb that signifies the redemption of Christ, for from Him we receive purity in our conduct.

"In the first month": that is, the month of Abib, and if a person was defiled for any reason, he keeps it in the following month on the fourteenth day (Num 6:6-13). He declared the importance of holding to the eating of unleavened bread, and whoever violates this is put to death, whether he is:
"A stranger": that is, the Jewish proselytes, who are those who joined the Jews and were circumcised, whether from the Egyptians or the Canaanites or any other people.
"Born in the land": he means the descendants of Jacob and their children, that is, the original Jews who are not proselytes, whose fathers were born in the land of Canaan, that is, the Promised Land.

The first Passover was kept in Egypt and the second in the wilderness of Sinai by Moses, and the third in Canaan by Joshua (Josh 5) after the forty years of wandering in the wilderness, and it was meant to be kept every year as God commanded.

Whoever disobeys and rejects God's commandment deserves death, but His mercy is longsuffering toward you, that perhaps you may repent, and it receives you and removes from you the sentence of death by the blood of Christ.

entries.section: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

paragraphs.text: Moses commanded all the people that each one should prepare a lamb to slaughter and offer as a Passover to the Lord.

entries.section: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

paragraphs.text: Hyssop: a plant like thyme, with stems bearing weak green leaves resembling the parsley plant. If the blood of the Passover lamb signifies the blood of Christ, that is, the work of grace, then the hyssop signifies human striving, which, despite its weakness like the leaves of hyssop, is necessary for receiving salvation.

Moses asked them, after the slaughter of the lamb, to pour its blood into a vessel of metal or earthenware called the basin (a small bowl or basin), then to bring a bunch or bundle of the hyssop plant and dip this bundle in the blood and strike with it the upper door post and its two side posts, right and left. He asked them on this night to take shelter inside their houses behind this door marked with blood, and so the destroying angel who would kill the firstborn of the Egyptians would not harm them.
Repentance, holding to God's commandments and partaking of His Holy Sacraments protect from God's judgment, and Satan cannot harm you.

entries.section: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

paragraphs.text: God passes through, by means of the destroying angel, and sees the blood that protects those inside the house and does not harm them, while the one who does not believe in God and has not struck his door with the blood is exposed to the killing of his firstborn.
If you believe, you live reassured, sheltered by God, and fears and anxiety are removed from you, and you live happy as well.

entries.section: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

paragraphs.text: He asked them to keep the Passover every year throughout their lives and after their entering the Promised Land.

entries.section: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

paragraphs.text: He asked them to teach their children the feast of the Passover, which is a memorial of God's protection of His children from evil, as happened in Egypt in that their firstborn were not killed. The people agreed and declared their submission by bowing down to God, and they went and did what Moses had said, and slaughtered the sheep and struck the doors with the blood.

entries.section: (4) The plague of the firstborn (the tenth plague)

paragraphs.text: After the children of Israel slaughtered the sheep and struck the doors with the blood, the destroying angel passed over their houses at midnight, but he entered all the houses of the Egyptians and killed their firstborn, whether the firstborn of the greatest man, who is Pharaoh, or the weakest man, who is the captive. It seems that the angel's entering was with a loud voice inside the house, which woke everyone, and he killed the firstborn, and the firstborn cried out, and all the members of his house, so there was a cry in all Egypt. And the firstborn, as he was dying, declared the reason for his death, which was the preventing of the children of Israel from going out, as stated in the deuterocanonical books (the Book of Wisdom 18:18).

entries.section: (4) The plague of the firstborn (the tenth plague)

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh hastened to summon Moses and Aaron during the night and begged them to go out with all the people of Israel and with their flocks to worship God as they wished; indeed, in his great terror he also asked them to bless him, that is, to pray for him, because he feared that their God would kill him.

entries.section: (4) The plague of the firstborn (the tenth plague)

paragraphs.text: A general feeling prevailed in Egypt that they were all exposed to death, so they urged the children of Israel to go out quickly, fearing them lest they die like their firstborn.

God is able to give you grace and awe in the eyes of others, even those who are hostile to you and wrong you, so that they submit to you and fear to wrong you. So do not be disturbed if their wrongs are prolonged, for your God sees everything and stops them at the proper time and turns all their evil to your benefit, and counts for you in heaven every endurance you have endured for His sake.
"Their kneadingtroughs": light wooden vessels.

Because of the Egyptians' urging the children of Israel to go out, they hurried to gather their belongings. Their dough was without leaven, so they carried their kneadingtroughs with the dough in them, and the rest they put in their clothes, that is, in sheets or robes, and tied them in bundles and carried them on their shoulders to leave Egypt quickly.

"Before it was leavened" does not mean that they were going to put leaven in it, because God commanded them to eat unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven, but to declare that the flour had been mixed with water only a few hours earlier and therefore could not have become leavened, and they were going to prepare it as cakes of unleavened bread after a few hours, that is, at the dawn of the new day.
The children of Israel carried out God's word, so they asked the Egyptians for gold and silver and also clothing, to borrow from them for their journey into the wilderness.

God gave the children of Israel awe and fear in the eyes of the Egyptians, so they gave them everything they asked, although they knew that they were going out into the desert and would not return and that what they had borrowed would not be given back to them, and they did this out of terror of the children of Israel. In this the children of Israel recovered something of their rights, for their partial spoiling of the Egyptians was a recovering of something of what the Egyptians had taken from them by forcing them into labor for many years.

Do not be disturbed if your rights have been lost for many years, for your God who cares for you will compensate you at the proper time and will give you what is better than them, namely spiritual gifts, so that you receive peace, consolation and rest, in addition to material blessings such as your protection from many dangers into which others may fall, and He gives you the opportunity to be joined to Him and to enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (6) The departure of the children of Israel from Egypt

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses, which is the province or district at one edge of which lies the city of Tanis, and they moved toward the southeast to the city of Succoth, whose meaning is tents (map 2), because many tents were pitched there, and Succoth is 15 km from Rameses. Rameses lies in the place of the present-day Sharqia governorate, and their direction was southeast, that is, toward present-day Ismailia and south of it. Rameses signifies the corruption from which the spiritual man must depart and go to Succoth, which is the tents, that is, become a stranger to the world and so find God.

The number of those who went out was 600 thousand men, and the women were slightly more than that, that is, about 800 thousand, in addition to the children under 18 years, who were about 500 thousand, and to them is added the mixed multitude, who were the slaves and non-Jews who believed in God and were circumcised and joined the Jews, about 100 thousand, so the total is approximately 2 million.
And with them was a large number of cattle, which God had blessed so that they became numerous, that they might offer sacrifices to Him as He wished.

The number (6) signifies the perfection of human work, because God completed the creation of the world in six days and on the sixth day created man, while the number (100) signifies the community and the number (1000) signifies eternity, so the symbolic meaning of 600 thousand is the perfection of the human work of the community believing in God, departing from Egypt, whose goal is life with God in the wilderness in order to obtain heavenly life.

You need to leave the places of sin and become a stranger to the world in order to see God. So give up your pleasure and comfort to find God, for many material things can occupy you and turn your inclinations and ambitions toward them; so set limits for them and use them in measure, that you may continue and grow in your love for God.

entries.section: (6) The departure of the children of Israel from Egypt

paragraphs.text: "Cakes" of bread: dough baked on stones heated by the rays of the sun, which they leave until it is done.
When they reached Succoth they pitched their tents and baked their dough on stones scattered in the desert, and the dough was unleavened, without leaven, because they had gone out of Egypt quickly.
Map (2)

entries.section: (7) The time of the departure of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: 1- This verse makes clear, in a definite way, that the length of the time the people of the children of Israel were in the land of Egypt was 430 years, especially since the prophet Moses expressed this matter precisely in his saying, "the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt" (v. 40) and then "at the end of the four hundred and thirty years" (v. 41). It is also noticed that the prophet Moses is an eyewitness of this period and lived the last part of it himself in Egypt with his people.
2- This period is also mentioned in two other places in the Bible as 400 years, and this is an approximation, but precisely it is 430 years as we have mentioned, and these two places are:
a- When God spoke to Abram in (Gen 15:13) and told him that his seed would be a stranger in a land that is not theirs for 400 years.
b- When Stephen spoke before his martyrdom (Acts 7:6) and said that the seed of Abraham would sojourn for 400 years in a strange land, where they would be enslaved.

3- St. Paul the Apostle mentions in (Gal 3:16, 17) that this period is 430 years, and because he says that it is from Abraham until Moses, who received the Law, some thought that it begins from Abraham until Moses, and therefore the period they spent in Egypt would be less than 430 years. But if we look closely at (Gal 3:16) we notice that he says "to Abraham and his seed," and by his seed is meant Jacob, who entered Egypt with his twelve sons and his grandchildren, and they spent 430 years there. At the same time, by the seed of Abraham is meant Christ, in whom is fulfilled the accomplishment of the promises of salvation in the fullness of time.

entries.section: (7) The time of the departure of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: On the night in which the angel killed the firstborn of Egypt, that is, the fifteenth day of the month of Abib, all the children of Israel went out, and He calls them "the hosts of the Lord" because they believe in Him and are submissive to Him in a serious life like soldiers.
You are a soldier of Christ against Satan, so hold fast to your spiritual weapons, and God is able to bring you out of all his schemes and snares.

entries.section: (7) The time of the departure of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The night of the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt is considered a great night, because in it the power of God was shown, which protects His children and delivers them from evil, so they should remember it and keep a feast for it and thank God for it.

It declares that the Passover belongs only to the circumcised Jews and that no stranger, sojourner or guest among them may eat of it, as happens now in the Church of the New Testament, for no one can partake of the Holy Sacraments except one who has received Baptism, which circumcision signifies. And the foreign slave whom the Jew buys and who lives in his house, he circumcises first so that he may join the faith, and then he eats of the Passover. This slave bought with silver signifies the believing person owned by Christ.

It makes clear that the household eats the Passover inside the house, as the faithful eat the Body and Blood of the Lord inside the Church, and do not take it out except in the case of the sick person unable to come to church.
It also requires that no bone of the Passover lamb be broken, as happened with Christ, for His bones were not broken but He died slaughtered, by internal bleeding.

The bones are the strong part inside the body, so they signify the truth and the faith that is not broken; then it is said of the saints that God keeps their bones, not one of them is broken, that is, their faith is firm and does not change (Ps 34:20). All the members of the household would gather inside the house, sheltered behind the blood struck on the door, and this means the oneness of the household and its taking shelter under the blood of Christ. They slaughtered the Passover the first time in their houses, then they slaughtered it before the tabernacle of the congregation after it was set up. And when the Temple was established in Canaan they would come to Jerusalem and slaughter it before the house of the Lord, because the Passover is one of the three great feasts at which all the males of the children of Israel had to appear at the house of the Lord, namely the feasts of the Passover, of Pentecost and of Tabernacles (Deut 16:5, 6, 16).

It decrees here that all the children of Israel keep the Passover, for it is the condition of their membership in the people of God, just as Communion is the condition of a Christian's membership in the Church.

Here He confirmed the necessity of circumcision as a condition for whoever eats the Passover, and this for the second time in the same passage because of the importance of the matter. And all the children of Israel obeyed this law, so God kept their firstborn and brought them out of Egypt on this night with great power.

Enjoy the greatest grace in existence, which is partaking of the Holy Sacraments, for it is the greatest power you receive and the one in which you are unique among all mankind, and it protects you and saves you from the devil's wars and carries you across to eternity. A comparison between the Passover lamb and the sacrifice of Christ, which is signified by the series The Passover lamb The sacrifice of Christ
1- A male (v. 5) A male
2- A lamb without blemish (v. 5) Christ is a lamb without blemish
3- Of the first year (v. 5) signifies the innocence, purity and vitality of Christ

4- It is kept from the tenth day until the fourteenth Christ remained in Jerusalem four days before in their houses (vv. 3-6) His crucifixion, from Monday of the Pascha (corresponding to the tenth of Nisan) until He was crucified on Friday, which is the fourteenth of Nisan.(
5- It is slaughtered between the two evenings, that is, between the third Christ gave up His spirit on the Cross at and the fifth in the evening, which is the ninth hour the ninth hour.
6- The doors are struck with blood, so that it protects those inside by the blood of Christ we are saved from death, that is, we do not the house (v. 7) perish but live in it.
7- The lamb is one of the clean animals (v. 5) Christ is pure and holy
8- The lamb was roasted with fire (vv. 8, 9) Christ passed through the sufferings alone and bore the fire of the divine wrath and redeemed us
9- The whole lamb is roasted, its head and its legs with Christ bore all the spiritual, psychological and its inwards (v. 9) and bodily sufferings.
10- Not a bone of it is broken (v. 46) The bones of Christ were not broken on the Cross
11- Unleavened bread was eaten with it (v. 8) Christ is pure and clean.
12- It is eaten with bitter herbs (v. 9) Christ bore the bitter sufferings on the Cross

13- They ate it standing, with their loins girded, The believers who eat the Body of Christ and with their staves in their hands and their shoes on their feet and His Blood are always ready to depart in readiness for their departure from Egypt (v. 11). from the world and enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

14 They ate it on the same night and left none of it Christ accomplished our redemption on the Cross in one until the morning (v. 10) day, and we eat His Body and Blood on the same day and leave none of it for the next day

15- God commanded them to keep the Passover as an everlasting ordinance Christ commanded His Church to offer the sacrifice of His Body the series The Passover lamb The sacrifice of Christ throughout their generations (vv. 14, 24, 25) and Blood throughout their life on earth.
16- Only the circumcised among the Jews ate it Only the believers in Christ who have received holy Baptism and the proselytes (vv. 43, 44, 48, 49) eat the Body and Blood of the Lord.
17- Both great and small ate of it, that is, all members of Both great and small eat the Body and Blood of Christ, that is, all the household (v. 4) the believers
18- All the Jews had to keep the Passover (v. 47) All the believers of the Church must partake of the Body and and share in eating it Blood of the Lord, that is, be in one fellowship.

19- No one who was defiled for any reason ate of it Only the penitent and those who have received the Sacrament of Confession (Num 6:6-9). partake of the Body and Blood of Christ. The consecration of the firstborn, the wandering of the people and God's leading.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: God commanded Moses to teach the people the sanctification of the firstborn son and likewise the firstborn of the beast. These had been killed among the Egyptians by the destroying angel, but the firstborn of God's people were redeemed by the Passover lamb, which is a symbol of Christ, and He purchased them with His blood, so they belong to Him; therefore He asks that they be set apart for Him.
The following is to be noted in the offering of the firstborn:
1- Every firstborn was redeemed by the payment of five shekels of silver.
2- The tribe of the Levites was a redemption for the firstborn of the children of Israel.
3- The firstborn of the children of Israel exceeded the tribe of the Levites by 273 souls, so the redemption of each one was five shekels of silver (Num 3:39-51).
4- The firstborn of clean animals are sacrificed to God, while unclean animals are redeemed with a lamb or have their necks broken (vv. 2, 12, 16).
5- The firstborn remains seven days, nourished by its mother's milk, and then is sacrificed.
6- The owner of the animal takes nothing from these firstborn, such as their wool, nor does he use them for work, but they are offered to God.
7- It is not permitted to vow the firstborn of animals, for they will necessarily be offered according to the Law.

Set apart for God the beginning of your day, your best times and your abilities, in addition to offering the firstfruits of your possessions; and if God chooses one of your children for consecration, encourage him.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: He reminded them of the day of their departure from Egypt, in which they had been enslaved for more than four hundred years (430 years). It signifies the bondage of sin, since Egypt was full of idols. So He asks them to be committed to eating unleavened bread, which signifies purity, and to reject leaven, which signifies evil, and to sanctify the firstborn and eat the Passover lamb.
When you repent and confess, be more careful to reject the sources of evil, remembering the humiliation of sin, so that you may keep away from everything that leads to it.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: He reminds them to be committed to the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread throughout their lives, not only in the wilderness but also after they settle in the Promised Land and the pagan peoples are around them, so that they do not care for their foreign ideas but hold fast to the Law of God.

It is understood that the month of Nisan is the month of Abib. The month of Abib was the seventh of the months of the year, but God made it the first month, as mentioned in (ch. 12:2). Thus the Hebrews came to have a civil year, by which political, civil and agricultural matters were reckoned, and another, religious year, which begins with the month of Abib and by which feasts and religious occasions are reckoned. There is a month in the present Coptic year called Abib, but it is different from the month of Abib that existed among the Hebrews. The month of Abib corresponded to the present months of March and April; that is, the departure of the children of Israel was in the spring, which is a suitable time for their journey out of Egypt in the desert.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: He affirms the commitment to eating unleavened bread for seven days and the removal of leaven, which signifies evil... The number "7" signifies the perfection of the work of the Holy Spirit; that is, we live our whole life in purity, keeping away from evil.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: "A sign on your hand": that is, you do it with care.
"A memorial between your eyes": you understand it, remember it and see it always, so that you may fulfill it.
"In your mouth": you teach your children by it.
He stresses to him the commitment to observing the Passover and Unleavened Bread throughout his life, and teaching their spiritual meanings to his children through the generations.

Take care to teach your children and loved ones the spiritual teachings, so that they love God and the Church and are bound to Him, and ignorance does not hinder them from God, but the sweetness of fellowship with God is shown, directly or indirectly, according to the circumstances around you.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: He reminds them to fulfill the law of offering the firstborn to God throughout their lives, when they go out of Egypt and then settle in the land of Canaan, and He commands them as follows:

1- Offering the firstborn of man (the opener of the womb), the male, to God by consecrating him to Him. This is what happened in the consecration of the tribe of Levi for the service of God instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel (Num 3:11).

2- The firstborn of man is redeemed by offering five holy shekels of silver for each firstborn, which is equal to about 75 grams of silver (Num 18:16), and this was before the males of the tribe of the Levites, who became instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel, were counted.
3- Offering the firstborn of the male animal to God as a sacrifice.

4- Unclean animals, such as the donkey, are redeemed by offering a lamb in place of their firstborn, and if it is not offered, the firstborn of the unclean animal is killed so that no one eats it. The Law that Moses received made clear the unclean animals and the clean animals, and it is understood from this, as we mentioned in the Book of Genesis, that clean and unclean animals were known before the Law of Moses; that is, the fathers had learned them from God.
5- The male is offered because he represents strength, for we offer to God the best we have, in addition to the fact that he signifies Christ, who is the firstborn among many brethren (Rom 8:29).

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: He stresses the importance of teaching the children God's care and His power, which brought His people out with a strong hand from the bondage of Egypt after the killing of their firstborn. The means of their deliverance was the sacrifice of the lamb for the redemption of the firstborn; therefore they redeem the firstborn of man and offer the firstborn of the animals to God. And they place the words of this Law in phylacteries, that is, pieces of leather or cloth fastened on the forehead and wrapped around the head, and they also fasten another on the hand at the forearm. The intention is that they think about this Law and act by it, for the head signifies thought and the hand signifies action.

God did not lead them north to the land of Palestine, that is, the Promised Land, but they went from Rameses, which is near the land of Goshen, to Succoth, and then from Succoth they went south toward the Red Sea. Succoth is on the road between present-day Ismailia and Suez (map 2, p. 93). God made them wander far from the Promised Land because He knew their spiritual weakness: if they faced war they would be afraid and return to the bondage of Egypt. Therefore He allowed them to wander in the wilderness so that their only reliance would be on God. There was a short road leading north to Arish and Rafah, taking about two weeks to reach Palestine, but they would not have been able to face war with the Canaanites because of the weakness of their faith at that time. When they had spent forty years in the wilderness, their faith grew and they were trained in spiritual striving, so they were able to enter the Promised Land and face the Canaanites.
Kill the afflictions that pass over you, for they may be the solution for the salvation of your soul; God knows your nature and keeps you away from evil by using some afflictions.

Joseph felt his estrangement in Egypt despite his great position, and that his bones must be buried in the Promised Land, which is a symbol of the heavenly Jerusalem. So Moses remembered Joseph's command and took his bones with him as he left Egypt, and most likely he also took the bones of Joseph's brothers and carried them to Shechem in Canaan (Acts 7:16).

It is good that you always remember the estrangement of the world, so that you think of the beauty of eternity and strive to attain it, and so care for your readings, your prayers and your repentance.

The son and Israel moved from Succoth to Etham, on the edge of the wilderness of Sinai and on its border (map 2, p. 93). Thus they were left without a helper, and God then showed His care for them and sent them a pillar of cloud that covered them over their heads and protected them from the scorching sun throughout the day. It moved ahead above them, and as they lifted their heads toward it, they walked behind it.

It is a symbol of Baptism, because the cloud is a quantity of water like the water of Baptism, which gives those baptized in it a new nature, guides them to life with God, and passes with them through the afflictions that the scorching sun represents.
And at night the pillar of cloud turned into a pillar of fire from earth to heaven, moving before them, lighting their way, frightening their enemies and protecting them.

Darkness signifies sin and spiritual blindness, which the pillar of fire removes, lighting for them the way of life with God. It is of fire because our God is a consuming fire, and the pillar of fire signifies His commandments, which guide us to life with Him. Let us therefore be cleansed from every sin so that we may be pleasing before Him, and be assured of His power, which protects us from our enemies, the demons.
The pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire remained with them throughout the days of the wilderness; so God guides us and protects us throughout our life in the wilderness of the world.
Put God before you from the beginning of every day, so that your heart may be at peace and you may fear Him, and so reject sin, meditate on His love and enjoy fellowship with Him.
The crossing of the Red Sea

entries.section: (1) God changes the direction of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: "Pi Hahiroth": it means a farm, and perhaps Pharaoh had a farm there. It is located near the Gulf of Suez.
"Migdol": it means a tower or a fortress, and perhaps Egypt had a garrison in it to defend it against enemies. It is located near the Gulf of Suez.
"Baal Zephon": it means Baal of watching, and perhaps there was a temple there for the god Baal. It is located west of Suez on the Red Sea.
"By the sea": that is, by the Red Sea, at the point from which they crossed the sea.

God commanded Moses that they should turn toward the south, and the pillar of cloud moved to lead the children of Israel not eastward toward the wilderness of Sinai but south, beside the Bitter Lakes, toward the Gulf of Suez. They reached a place beside the Gulf of Suez, that is, before the sea near present-day Suez, most likely about ten miles south of Suez, and the width of the sea there is about eight miles. This distance is enough to hold all the people of Israel and then the army of the Egyptians after them.

entries.section: (1) God changes the direction of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: "The wilderness hath shut them in": they became hemmed in in a dry desert, not knowing where to go, as if they were in a building that had been shut upon them.
News of the movements of the children of Israel will reach Pharaoh through his spies, and he will learn of the change of their course and think that they are bewildered.

entries.section: (1) God changes the direction of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: "I will harden Pharaoh's heart": God uses Pharaoh's pride, so that the king hardens his heart.
Pharaoh and his army will pursue the children of Israel to bring them back to Egypt to serve him, and so the glory of God will be shown in the victory over him.

Do not be troubled by the increasing power of the wicked, for it is temporary, and God will give you victory in the end, because their power is nothing before God. God is long-suffering toward them, that perhaps they may repent, and so that your faith may be established and you may receive more abundant blessings.

entries.section: (2) Pharaoh regrets letting the children of Israel go

paragraphs.text: After the departure of the children of Israel, Pharaoh felt his loss at the disappearance of this great number of workers in his service, and he regretted letting them go. Indeed he wanted to bring them back, and his servants and counselors encouraged him in this.

entries.section: (2) Pharaoh regrets letting the children of Israel go

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh set out with his war chariot and the men of his army to bring back the children of Israel.

entries.section: (2) Pharaoh regrets letting the children of Israel go

paragraphs.text: "Captains over every one of them" (literally, his charioteer soldiers): the soldiers trained to ride in war chariots and to fight the enemies from them.

"Chariot": a vehicle of iron and wood drawn by horses, in which the soldiers ride, so that they can run swiftly. Pharaoh took with him 600 war chariots, the soldiers trained to drive them, and a great army that was distinguished from the armies of the surrounding countries in the whole world.

The number (6) points to the whole perfection of human work, and the number (100) points to the perfection of the work of the community; that is, (600) means the utmost strength of man, especially since Pharaoh was the strongest of the kings of the earth at that time.

It is noted that some of the horses had died in the plague of hail while others lived, because those of the Egyptians who feared God had hidden their cattle, in addition to the purchase of other horses from the neighboring countries to replace what was lost, so that their armies would be complete and ready for war.

entries.section: (2) Pharaoh regrets letting the children of Israel go

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh hurried with his army toward the children of Israel and overtook them while they were before the Red Sea, south of Suez.
If you have kept away from sin, do not return to it through the hardness of your heart, lest this be your last opportunity and you perish in sin.

entries.section: (3) The terror of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: When the children of Israel saw the greatness of the Egyptian army, they were very afraid, so they prayed to God with all their hearts, crying out that He would rescue them from this death or bondage.

entries.section: (3) The terror of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel murmured against Moses because they felt that their destruction before the Egyptians was certain, since they saw the sea before them and the armies of the Egyptians behind them. They were convinced that their death was certain, and they rebuked Moses for not leaving them in the bondage of the Egyptians.
Do not yield to sin, however difficult it may seem; it is better for you to die while striving than to yield to it.

entries.section: (3) The terror of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Moses reassured them that the Lord would fight for them and defeat the Egyptians, and their threats and fear would vanish. He said all this by faith; perhaps God had informed him that he would triumph and be saved from the hand of the Egyptians, who would die, and that no harm would touch him and his people, so he believed the word of God.
By faith you can see what others do not see, and so you live in peace.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: Moses prayed in silence and God heard him; indeed He counted his deep, quiet prayer as a cry, so He reassured him and asked him to bring the people near to the sea.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: He commanded him to strike the sea with the rod so that it would divide into two halves and the children of Israel would cross on dry ground in the midst of the sea.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: He told him of the hardness of Pharaoh's heart, who would not benefit from the miracle of the parting of the sea but would pursue the children of Israel even into the sea. He told him this to reassure him when he saw Pharaoh pursuing them inside the sea, and He commanded him to wait for the power of God, which would triumph over him.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: God's purpose is not only to save His people but also the faith of the Egyptians when they see the defeat of their king and his army and their death.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: It is declared here that the pillar of cloud or the pillar of fire is an angel of God who protects His people. The cloud used to cover the children of Israel to protect them from the heat of the sun, and now it turned into a pillar from earth to heaven separating the people of God from the Egyptians to protect them, so that the Egyptians could not see the people of God because of the mist. This was for the protection of the people of God and a warning to the Egyptians, that they might believe and turn back from pursuing the children of Israel. It is understood from this that the parting of the Red Sea took place in the daytime before the sun set.
Learn from God's warnings, so that you do not persist in your sin but return by repentance, and He will save you.

entries.section: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

paragraphs.text: "The one to the other": the Egyptians to the children of Israel.

The pillar of cloud continued to separate the children of Israel from the Egyptians, and when night fell it turned into a pillar of fire, so the Egyptians were afraid and could not approach or harm the children of Israel.

entries.section: (5) The crossing of the sea by the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Moses struck the sea with the rod, and it divided into two halves by a strong east wind, and the bed of the sea appeared as dry land.
The rod signifies the Cross, which opens a way for you in the midst of the world, that is, the sea, so that you walk in peace.

entries.section: (5) The crossing of the sea by the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel advanced and walked on the ground, with the water like a wall to them on the right and on the left. They trusted in God who protected them, so they were not afraid of the water that stood miraculously like a wall on both sides of them.

entries.section: (5) The crossing of the sea by the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Because of Pharaoh's hardness, he pursued the children of Israel into the sea and did not repent or learn anything from the miracle. The distance over which the children of Israel walked in the divided sea was about seven miles, at a place south of Suez. This long distance allowed about 2 million people to cross in it, followed by a great, mighty army of the Egyptians.

entries.section: (5) The crossing of the sea by the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: "The morning watch": that is, the time of daybreak, which is the end of the night, because the children of Israel crossed the Red Sea throughout the night, and at its end the pillar of fire moved and drew near to Pharaoh's horses and chariots. The horses were afraid and did not want to advance, so they drove them forward with great difficulty.
"Looked unto the host of the Egyptians": God looked upon them and troubled them with the pillar of fire that drew near to them, and they were very afraid.

"Took off their chariot wheels": the wheels of his strong iron chariots came off, because of the horses drawing back and the soldiers striking them to advance, so the chariots swayed and some of their wheels came off.

When God saw the hardness of Pharaoh's heart, He moved the pillar of fire toward his horsemen and chariots, and his strongest horses were afraid, and some of the army began to feel the power of God that protects His people, so they tried to flee and draw back. But Pharaoh's orders were strict to continue the attack and keep pursuing the children of Israel, and this was the last opportunity God gave them for repentance. It is noted that the Egyptians felt that the God of Israel was very strong and was fighting for His people, so they were troubled, but unfortunately they did not believe with the faith that calls to repentance and turning back; rather, their faith was like the faith of the demons in God, that is, they were insisting on their sin, so they perished. Even if they tried to flee, it was out of panic and fear, but they did not truly believe in God.
Repentance in words is not enough, but it must be carried out with swift striving, because your negligence will bring disgrace upon you.

After the children of Israel had come out of the sea and were in the wilderness, while the whole army of the Egyptians was inside the sea and the pillar of fire was still before them inside the sea, separating them from the children of Israel, God commanded Moses to strike the sea with his rod so that it would return as it was, and it covered the whole army of the Egyptians, and all of them died.
The children of Israel had crossed the sea walking on dry ground and then came out of the sea into the wilderness of Sinai.

In the morning the children of Israel found themselves safe in the wilderness, and then the sea cast up many of the bodies of the Egyptians on the shore, because all of them had died; some of their bodies were on the bottom and some were thrown by the waves onto the shore.
Before the mighty power of God, the faith of His people in Him was established, and they submitted to their great leader in faith, Moses.
Look at God's works with you and meditate on them, so that your faith in Him may be established and you may submit to His commandments. The Tasbeha (praise) and going to Marah and Elim

Moses led the people in praise and glorified God for His great power in His victory over the enemies and the protection of His people, despite the strength of the Egyptian army with its chariots and horsemen, as they all drowned in the sea. This is the first song of praise to the Lord in the Holy Bible, written by Moses, and it speaks of two subjects:
1- God's rescue of His people and the destruction of their enemies (vv. 1-12).
2- A prophecy of their entering Canaan and their victory over its inhabitants (vv. 13-20).
Because of Moses' love for God, he loved praising Him until God became his glorification and his joy, so he blessed Him and declared his faith in Him above all the pagan gods.

The power of God appeared as a warrior greater than all the warriors of the earth, so His name became the greatest of warriors, that is, able to triumph in all wars however strong the enemies may be.
