This does not contradict His being the God of heaven, because He disciplines the enemies that perhaps they may repent, and if they exhaust all opportunities for repentance, He destroys them, that perhaps whoever sees them may believe and return to God and enjoy His fatherly tenderness and mercy.
The strongest army in the world at that time, the Egyptian army, with its chariots and horses of which it boasts, was drowned.
"The depths": the waves.
The bodies of the enemies sank like a stone to the bottom of the sea, and they became like stone because their hearts were of stone and refused to believe in God.
The right hand represents power, so the power of God is stronger than all the enemies, who signify the demons, and we no longer fear their wars.
God's wrath against the wicked consumes them quickly, and He likened them to stubble in the swiftness of its burning.

"The blast of thy nostrils": He likens God to a man with a nose from which breath goes out, and because God is strong, His breath is very strong; what is meant is the east wind that dried the sea so that the children of Israel crossed over it. "The waters were gathered together": they began to rise one upon another to become like a wall on both sides.
"The floods stood upright": the flowing waters stood upright like a wall on both sides.
"As an heap": the raised hill.
"The depths were congealed": the waves became solid like a dry wall inside the sea.

God sent an east wind that divided the Red Sea, so the waters congealed like a wall on both sides so that the people of God might cross in safety. Thus the power of God that works miracles appears, giving the waters a new nature that is not their own, which is to stand vertically like a wall, and this is against the law of the earth's gravity for liquids. God has done many miracles of this kind, among them His walking, and Peter's, on the water (Mt 14:26, 29).

Pharaoh dared in his wickedness to follow the people of God to seize them and return them as slaves to him in Egypt and to kill whoever opposed him, thinking that he was able to overtake them and bring them back as spoil for himself, they and all that was with them. So Satan dares against the children of God, but they defeat him by the power of God.
God commanded, and the sea returned as it was after the children of Israel had come out, so the Egyptians drowned and became heavy as lead and clung to the earth as if they were earthly and carnal.

God is greater than all the pagan gods in His holiness... praised above all, a worker of miracles that the mind cannot imagine; His servants praise Him with fear, while His enemies tremble and shudder.
God stretched out His hand over the sea and it covered the Egyptians, and the sea swallowed them up and they sank to its bottom.

God rescued His children from the bondage of Egypt and brought them out to the wilderness of Sinai to worship Him in the tabernacle of meeting, where His holy sanctuary is. He guided them by His mercies and His fatherly tenderness, and had compassion on them because of their faith and their sense of their weakness. He redeemed them by bringing them out of the bondage of Egypt by means of the Passover lamb and His killing of the firstborn of Egypt, and He guided them to walk in the wilderness to Mount Sinai, where He declared to them the commandments and the tabernacle of meeting, and they set it up there.
All the nations heard of this miracle, such as the land of Palestine, that is, the land of Canaan, which the children of Israel possessed afterward, and they were very afraid of God and His people.

God gives His children awe in the eyes of others, as they feel a wonderful power in them and fear to wrong them despite their weak appearance, because God protects them and makes their enemies fear them.

He gives examples of the inhabitants of the Promised Land, namely the Edomites, the Moabites and the Canaanites, who were afraid when they heard of the crossing of the Red Sea and the drowning of the Egyptians.
"Thou hast purchased": by Your bringing Your people out of the bondage of Egypt to become a people of Your own.

All the peoples of the earth were afraid and became silent as a stone before the power of God that appeared in His people when they crossed the wilderness of Sinai and entered the Promised Land, and when they crossed the Red Sea by a divine miracle and the strongest army in the world, the army of the Egyptians, died before them. This prophecy was fulfilled by the defeat of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, and Balak king of Moab was troubled by them (Num 21:1-3).

The children of Israel did not come out of the bondage of Egypt to live in the wilderness of Sinai but to possess and be established in the land of Canaan, and to build the temple in Jerusalem on Mount Zion to worship the Lord all their days, and that God might reign over the hearts of His children, and that there might come from them Christ, who reigns forever.

He presents the summary of the miracle, which is the drowning of the whole Egyptian army and the deliverance of the children of Israel, who crossed into the wilderness of Sinai by walking on dry ground in the midst of the sea.
God is able to perform any miracle to rescue and keep His people in every generation, so be at peace and hold fast to your prayers, confident in the power of your God.

"The sister of Aaron": she was called so because Aaron was the older in age, although Moses was more famous than he, and out of Moses' humility he did not attribute his sister to himself but to his brother.

"Timbrels": round frames of wood with a thin skin stretched over one of their faces, with metal discs fixed to them, so that when struck against the wall these discs or small cymbals move and produce a strong sound and clear tones.

"Dances": calm movements offered as worship to God, which were used anciently to express joy and praise to God, as David danced before the ark of the covenant (2 Sam 6:14). This is of course entirely different from worldly dancing, which God hated and because of which Moses destroyed those who danced around the golden calf (ch. 32). The women also took part, led by Miriam the sister of Moses, in praising God, using timbrels as musical instruments to express their joy.
Miriam was leading them in praise like Moses her brother, magnifying and blessing God who triumphed over His enemies.

Because of the importance of this praise that Moses spoke and Miriam his sister followed in it, the Church takes care to repeat it every day in her Tasbeha and calls it the First Hoos, that is, the first praise, because it declares the power of God with His faithful children, which gives them victory over the demons, gives them spiritual blessings and then brings them into heaven.
"Shur": it means a wall, and it lies north of the wilderness of Sinai, and Etham is on its edge, so it is sometimes called the wilderness of Etham, as in (Num 33:6-8) (map 2, p. 93).

After the people had glorified God and rejoiced in freedom, they walked three days in the barren wilderness of Sinai, led by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night, that is, God was leading them, until they reached the wilderness of Shur, a barren wilderness with no water or grass.
"Marah": a wilderness whose waters are bitter even now, lying south of the Springs of Moses near the northeastern bank of the Gulf of Suez.
The children of Israel reached a wilderness in which there were springs of water, but it was bitter and could not be drunk because of its bitterness, so they called it Marah.
The people felt great distress, as they almost died of thirst, and they murmured against Moses their leader and against God.
The servant is responsible for those he serves and must bear their murmurings and pray for them, so that God may satisfy them, shepherd them and solve their problems.
"There": in Marah.
"There he made for them a statute and an ordinance": that is, the commandment that God spoke in the next verse.
"And there he proved them": He allowed them the affliction of the bitter water to show their faith in God or their murmuring.

Moses prayed by the power of God, and He answered him and instructed him to cast a tree, or a branch of it, into the bitter water, and it became sweet, and the people drank of it and were satisfied. Thus Moses passed the test successfully because of his faith and his prayer, while the people showed their weakness in their murmuring and lack of faith. And as he cast the tree into the water and it was buried in it and made it sweet, so by the burial of Christ in the tomb He raised us from death and gave us a new, sweet life with Him. The tree signifies the Cross that accomplished our redemption, so we were satisfied with the Holy Spirit, and the placing of the tree in the water signifies the sacrament of Baptism that we received from the blessings of the Cross.

God charged the people through Moses to listen to the commandments of God after they had seen His power for the second time since the miracle of the crossing of the Red Sea, and He asked them to obey Him so that they would not be exposed to the diseases that fell on the Egyptians in the ten plagues, but that God would heal them of every disease they might be exposed to, as He healed the bitter water so that it became sweet.
"Elim": it means trees, and it is a fertile oasis lying southeast of Marah, that is, inside the wilderness of Sinai and not far from the Gulf of Suez.

After the trial of the bitter water, God led them to a fertile region, Elim, in which there were 12 springs of water and which was full of trees, for there were seventy palm trees in it. They signify the twelve tribes and the seventy elders in the Jewish supreme council (the Sanhedrin), and they signify even more the grace of the New Testament, in which there are 12 disciples and 70 apostles.
If you endure the trial, you receive blessings from God that you do not expect, so you are satisfied and refreshed by His grace and rejoice with a true joy.
The manna and the quails

entries.section: (1) The hunger and murmuring of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: "The wilderness of Sin": it is a desert region lying between Elim on the west and the wilderness of Sinai on the east (map 2, p. 93). What is meant by the wilderness of Sinai is the middle part of the wilderness of Sinai extending east of Suez to the borders of the land of Sinai. The wilderness of Sinai mentioned here extends from the middle to near the south of Sinai. The cloud moved from Elim and they reached the wilderness of Sin as they were walking beside the Red Sea, and there was no food in it. The dough with which they had come out of the land of Egypt had run out, so they became hungry. This was in the second month on the fifteenth day, whereas their departure from the land of Egypt was on the fifteenth day of the first month; that is, they reached the wilderness of Sin about a month after their departure.
The details of the journey in the wilderness of Sinai are found in the Book of Numbers (Num 33).

entries.section: (1) The hunger and murmuring of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron instead of praying, trusting in the power of God who had brought them across the sea.

entries.section: (1) The hunger and murmuring of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The people spoke to Moses and Aaron and rebuked them for the lack of food and their exposure to death, and they regretted leaving Egypt, remembering the meat and bread they used to eat there and forgetting the humiliation of bondage.
Do not seek the places of sin, however rich they may be or however great their material benefits, and however great your need; death with Christ is better than life in sin.

God answered the people's murmuring with blessings that cannot be imagined: food coming down from heaven in a very huge quantity covering the ground, so that all the people would be satisfied. Moreover, the food coming down from heaven is given daily, so that a man takes of it what suffices him for the one day. By this God tests the people, whether they will believe His word and obey Him, so that no one stores any of this food, or whether they will disobey Him and not be content with the need of the day. God's testing of His people for forty years in the wilderness after their being baptized in the cloud signifies the temptation of Christ for forty days in the wilderness after His Baptism at the hand of John the Baptist, and as the children of Israel entered the Promised Land after crossing the wilderness, so Christ also began His ministry of preaching and drawing souls after His temptation in the wilderness.

"They shall prepare that which they bring in": they make it ready for eating by grinding it and baking it or cooking it in any form (Num 11:8). God commands them to gather on the sixth day enough for two days, so that they may rest on the seventh day and be free for the worship of God.

Moses and Aaron knew that God would give meat in the evening, which is the quails (v. 13), coming in great migrating flocks from Europe to central Africa, passing through the wilderness of Sinai in great weariness and flying close to the ground at a height of about one meter, so that they are easy to catch because they fly slowly. This matter of the quails happened either (1) for one day at the beginning of their entering Sinai and then, years later, for a month in the region of Taberah (Num 11), or (2) their words here are about what would happen later, when they ask for meat and He gives them the quails; the details of this story are mentioned in (Num 11). But in the morning of this day, and throughout the forty years, the manna came down like rain from heaven.

Moses made clear to them that God would give them meat in the evening, which is the quails, and bread, which is the manna, in the morning, and he declared that he was merely a mediator between them and God, who had heard their murmuring and answered with His tenderness and gave them their needs.
Moses and Aaron proclaimed the presence of God and His hearing of the people's murmuring, and asked them to rise and come forward to hear the voice of God.
God is present, but you do not feel His presence unless you draw near to Him in prayer, and then you receive His blessings and He forgives you your sins.

While Aaron was speaking to the people of what God had commanded him and Moses, and announcing to them the coming down of food from heaven, the glory of God appeared in the cloud; that is, a great cloud, attracting attention, appeared.

God spoke from the cloud and the people heard His voice, and perhaps they distinguished the words, or Moses and Aaron did, and told the people that God would give them meat in the evening, which is the quail bird. The flocks of quails came twice: the first time at the beginning of the people's departure into the wilderness, and the second time for a month when they murmured against God because they were weary of the manna, and that was at Taberah. In the morning, God gave them the manna, that is, the bread coming down from heaven.
God is long-suffering toward you and answers your murmurings with blessings, that perhaps you may believe in Him, thank Him and apologize for your murmuring.

entries.section: (3) The coming down of the quails and the manna

paragraphs.text: "Came up": flew at a height of about one meter from the ground (Num 11:31). "Quails": a bird resembling the quail and the size of a dove, but its neck and legs are longer than the neck and legs of a dove.

What God had said was indeed done, as flocks of quails passed in the evening of the same day, and the people took of them as they wished. In the morning the dew, which carries the manna, covered the wilderness around the children of Israel.

entries.section: (3) The coming down of the quails and the manna

paragraphs.text: In the morning the dew evaporated, and the people found a fine thing covering the ground, resembling flakes or brittle frost, and white in color.

entries.section: (3) The coming down of the quails and the manna

paragraphs.text: The people asked about this thing that covered the ground, and Moses said to them, it is the food that God has given you; therefore it was called manna, and because they did not know what it was they said, "Who is it?"
The manna is a symbol of Christ in the following:
1- The manna came down from heaven, as Christ became incarnate and descended from His heaven to live in our midst.
2- The manna is white, as Christ is pure, without sin.
3- The taste of the manna is sweet, like the words of Christ, sweet to the soul.

4- The manna came down after the murmuring of the Jews because they had no food, and it made peace and satisfied them, as Christ by His Incarnation and redemption made reconciliation between God and mankind.

5- The manna came down in the early morning, and the people went out to gather it, or else it melted with the rays of the sun; likewise whoever wants to live with Christ must rise early to Him and put Him before all his worldly concerns.

6- A man gathers of the manna what suffices him for his daily food, just as the Christian must be content in meeting his material needs, not busying himself with storing up or worrying about the future, because he is satisfied with Christ, who satisfies him even if what he has of material things is little.
7- Whoever gathers of the manna more than he needs and keeps it for the next day, it spoils; likewise whoever does not use the means of grace that he knows and the word of God, it condemns him.

8- The people did not know this food, so they said, "Who is it?"; likewise no one can know the essence of Christ, but we know something of His attributes and His relation to us as far as we can understand.
9- They would bake it or cook it, that is, they used fire in cooking it; and Christ also bore sufferings to offer us salvation and spiritual satisfaction.

entries.section: (3) The coming down of the quails and the manna

paragraphs.text: Moses commanded them to take what they needed of this food, and he told them that each one should take the measure of an omer, which equals 2.29 liters, that is, about two and a third liters.

God's gifts may seem strange at first because they are higher than worldly blessings, but when you obey God and thank Him, you discover their sweetness more and more. God's arrangements may seem strange or contrary to your planning, but if you accept them with contentment, you discover in time that they are the best thing for you, and satisfy you, and suit your life and lead you toward God.
Each one gathered as much as he wished of this food; some gathered much and some little.

The surprise appeared when each one measured what he had gathered in order to carry out God's commandment to gather an omer for every person, and they discovered that what they had gathered was an omer for each individual, whether they had gathered much or little.
When God blesses your works, He gives you good enough for you, and even if it seems little, you will be satisfied with it.

Moses commanded them not to leave any of it until the next morning, but some of them doubted the coming down of the manna the next day and kept some of it, but were surprised to find it full of worms and loathsome, not to be eaten, so Moses was angry with them because of the weakness of their faith and their disobedience to God.
The people continued to gather every day what they needed of the manna. The strange thing is that when the sun rose the manna melted and became liquid, and the earth drank it.
If you do not rise early to God to receive His blessing in prayer, the blessing may depart from you and your opportunity be lost, as the manna would melt and be gone.

entries.section: (5) The manna does not come down on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The people obeyed and gathered on the sixth day twice what they gathered on the other days, because the manna would not come down on the Sabbath. The rulers of the people told Moses what they had done, to make sure that this was the command of the Lord, so that he would not be angry with them as happened when some of them kept some of it until the next day and it bred worms (v. 20).

entries.section: (5) The manna does not come down on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: Moses said to them, cook it so that you may eat of it in the way you wish, and keep the rest until the next day, and it will not spoil, so that you may be free on the seventh day for the worship of God.

Take care of Sunday, the Lord's Day, and increase your prayers and good works, remembering that on this day Christ rose to give you a new life; make it a day distinguished from the rest of your days, so that you may feel God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (5) The manna does not come down on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: God's word was indeed fulfilled, that the manna that was kept would not spoil with stench or worms the next day, that is, the Sabbath.

entries.section: (5) The manna does not come down on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: Moses told them to eat of the manna that was kept on the Sabbath, because no manna would come down on this day; so this became a custom with them, to rest on the seventh day to be free for worship.
Be sure that God provides for your needs, and your being occupied with His worship will not diminish the material blessing but will increase it.

entries.section: (6) The people's disobedience in going out to gather the manna

paragraphs.text: Some of the Jews did not believe God's word and went out to make sure for themselves that there was no manna on the seventh day. This shows their doubt of God's commands and their attachment to material things.

entries.section: (6) The people's disobedience in going out to gather the manna

paragraphs.text: "Abide ye every man in his place": what is meant is that they should not go out in the morning to gather manna but be free on this day for the worship of God, leaving all material work, moving only short distances if necessary, as the elders of the Jews determined.
God reproached the people in His speech with Moses because they had gone out on the Sabbath to gather manna although He had commanded them not to go out, so He rebuked their disobedience.

entries.section: (6) The people's disobedience in going out to gather the manna

paragraphs.text: After this incident the whole people obeyed the word of God and did not move on the Sabbath to gather manna.

entries.section: (6) The people's disobedience in going out to gather the manna

paragraphs.text: He describes the taste of the manna as sweet, like wafers made with honey, and its form as small grains like coriander seed. The Book of Wisdom tells us how every person who ate the manna felt a particular taste as he desired, and this is a wonderful mystery, that the manna had different tastes according to the desire of each one.
Believe the word of the Holy Bible even if it is above your mind, and do not transgress its commandments, so that you may enjoy its blessings and God's pleasure with you.
"A pot": a vessel.
"The testimony": the ark of the covenant in the tabernacle of meeting.

God commanded Moses that they keep a quantity of manna in a vessel, so that throughout history they would remember the miracle of the Lord in feeding them in the wilderness. They kept the manna afterward in a golden vessel inside the ark of the covenant. The quantity of manna that was kept was the measure of an omer, that is, about 2.29 liters.
The keeping of the manna in the golden pot signifies:
1- The Incarnation of Christ, for as the manna came down from heaven, God came down and became incarnate in the fullness of time.
2- The manna signifies Holy Communion from the Body and Blood of Christ.
3- The golden pot signifies the Virgin who carried Christ in her womb.

God continued to send the manna daily to feed His people for 40 years in the wilderness of Sinai until they reached the Promised Land, where they found cultivated land and ate of its fruits, and the manna ceased. Moses said this by the spirit of prophecy, for the manna ceased when Joshua entered the Promised Land and they began to eat the fruits of the land; in addition, it may have ceased for the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, who took possession east of the Jordan in the days of Moses (Num 32, Josh 13).

God's gifts to you continue as long as you feel your need of them, but when you find material things to lean on, God stops His gifts. So do not be distressed by the lack of some resources or the fewness of friends and loved ones, because God Himself compensates you for them, and He is your true strength and your personal friend.
The omer equals, as we mentioned, 2.29 liters, and it is a tenth of a known Jewish measure, the ephah, which equals 22.9 liters.
The symbols of the manna: we note from the above that the manna signifies:
1- The Incarnation of Christ, for He said of Himself, "I am the living bread which came down from heaven" (Jn 6:51).

2- The Body and Blood of Christ, for He said, "the bread that I will give is my flesh" (Jn 6:51). And He also said, "Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you" (Jn 6:53).
3- It is the glory that we receive in heaven, for He said, "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna" (Rev 2:17). The spiritual meanings of the manna:
1- Faith and reliance on God, who provides for our needs daily.

2- Obedience to God, whose commands exceed our mental comprehension: their going out every day to gather the manna, not keeping any of it for the next day except on the sixth day, and not going out on the seventh day.
3- Rising early to God before any work, in prayer and reading His Holy Bible, as they used to rise early before sunrise to gather the manna before it melted in the heat of the sun.
4- The importance of work and spiritual striving, which appeared in their going out every morning to gather it.
5- The blessing of God, for what each person gathered was enough, whether he gathered little or much.

6- God's keeping of our food and our needs, for the manna, which melts in the light rays of the sun in the early morning, remains firm and produces different cakes and baked goods after the women put it on the strong fire (Wis 16:27).

7- The variety of God's blessings to man so that he may delight in them, for the taste of the manna for each one who ate it was according to what he desired, that is, its flavor differed from one person to another according to the liking of each one (Wis 16:25).

8- Contentment, for God gave them one food and did not give them different kinds of foods, and because of their contentment He made His food differ according to the desire of each one. This is what calls the faithful to fasting and detachment, so that God blesses the little they have and it becomes sweet and satisfying to them. The bringing forth of water from the rock and the defeat of Amalek

"According to their journeys": the children of Israel traveled as groups, each group pitching its tents beside the other, and when they moved from place to place they moved one group after another, and also according to the places through which they passed and from which God commanded them to move on to another.
Rephidim: its meaning is resting places, and it is in the middle of the wilderness of Sinai toward the south.
The children of Israel moved from the wilderness of Sin southward to a place called Rephidim, and it was barren, with no water in it.

The people murmured against Moses because of their thirst and demanded that he and Aaron bring water, and he rebuked them for their murmuring against God after they had seen great wonders such as the ten plagues, the crossing of the Red Sea, the turning of the bitter water into sweet water at Marah, and the sending of the manna and the quails...
The people fell not only into murmuring but also into despair because of the severity of the thirst, but sadly they did not lift up their prayers to God, as they felt that they would die of thirst.

Because of the people's great agitation and murmuring, Moses was afraid and cried out to God to save him from their hands, because they were almost ready to stone him. This shows Moses' faith in his taking refuge in God, but there is in him some weakness of faith because of his fear of the people.
Take refuge in God in all your afflictions, however harsh, and even if all people rise up against you, trust that He is able to save you and to work miracles for you.

God answered Moses and promised to solve the problem by his going on before the people with his rod, so that they might be reassured that God was with him, because God had worked many miracles with this rod, and He commanded him to take with him some of the elders of the children of Israel to be witnesses of the miracle that would happen, which was the coming out of water from the solid rock.
The rock: it was a rock known to Moses, which was either beside the bush or beside which the pillar of fire used to stand.
Horeb: the name of the region in which Mount Sinai lies.

God commanded Moses to strike the rock so that water would come out, and he did so, and the water came out before the elders of Israel. The rock signifies Christ, who quenches our thirst with the waters of His Holy Spirit. The rod signifies the Cross that Christ bore for us: the rod struck the rock, and likewise through His crucifixion we received the Holy Spirit. The rod also signifies the Law, which Christ fulfilled and then died and redeemed us, and it also signifies the spear with which Christ was pierced on the Cross, and blood and water came out of His side.
Meribah: chiding.
Massah: temptation.
Another place at Kadesh was also called by this name (Num 20:13) because of the likeness of what happened there to this incident.

Moses called the place where the water came out of the rock Massah and Meribah, to remind the people that they had fallen into temptation and murmured and quarreled with God, but God in His tenderness gave them water.
Remember your sins at all times so that you may always repent, and so thank God and receive His mercies.

Amalek: they are the descendants of Eliphaz the son of Esau, and there was enmity between them and the descendants of Jacob, perhaps because of Jacob's taking the birthright from their forefather Esau. They lived in the south of Palestine and Syria, and they were enraged when they saw God's blessing in the number of the children of Israel, so they attacked them.

Joshua: he is the son of Nun of the tribe of Ephraim, and the meaning of his name is God saves; he was one of the spies whom Moses sent to spy out the Promised Land (Num 13, 14) and became Moses' successor in leading the people and bringing them into the Promised Land (Num 13:8). An army of tall men attacked them in the wilderness of Sinai for the first time, and they called them Amalekites. So Moses sent Joshua to lead the army and fight Amalek, while he went up on a hill to pray for them and held in his hand the rod of God, to strengthen the people's faith in God, who had worked many miracles for him with this rod, and so that he might ask Him to intervene for victory over Amalek.
Joining your spiritual striving with your prayer guarantees you victory, so do not fear your enemies, however mighty, as long as you are faithful in your works and pray.

Hur: one of Moses' close disciples, of the tribe of Judah, and the grandfather of Bezaleel, who led the craftsmen who made the tabernacle of the congregation (Ex 31:1); some think that he was the husband of Miriam, the sister of Moses.
Joshua obeyed Moses and led the people to fight Amalek, while Moses went up the hill with his brother Aaron and one of Moses' pious disciples, Hur, to help him in prayer.
Important spiritual meanings appear from this, which are:
1- The importance of prayer accompanying spiritual striving.
2- The people's sharing with the leader or servant in prayer and every spiritual work, for this cooperation encourages souls and God rejoices in this unity.
3- Despite the strength of the leader or servant, he needs the help of other servants, namely Aaron and Hur, in addition to Joshua and all who fight with him.

How sweet it is for brethren to gather together for prayer, for God rejoices in the prayer of the congregation more than in the prayer of the individual; so would that you would take care to have common prayer in your home, if not every day then at least every week.

In prayer Moses lifted up his hands, so that he was in the form of a cross, and by the Cross and prayer Israel prevailed over Amalek. When he grew tired and his hands dropped a little, Amalek prevailed over Israel; so he strengthened himself and lifted up his hands again, and Israel regained its victory over the enemies, and then if he grew tired and his hands dropped, Amalek would return and prevail. God permitted this to declare the importance of joining prayer with the Cross, in whose form Moses was when he lifted up his hands to pray.
From this it appears that Moses here was a type of Christ in the following:
1- Moses lifted up his hands for prayer like Christ, who lifted up His hands on the Cross.

2- Moses' bodily weakness appeared and he needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his hands, and Christ in the garden of Gethsemane, when He was crushed with pain as a man, was visited by an angel to strengthen Him.
3- The rod in Moses' hand was a banner for the people to confirm their faith, and the Cross is the sign of victory for Christians.
4- Moses kept his hands stretched out until the going down of the sun, like Christ, who remained crucified until He died at the ninth hour, and they took His body down at sunset.
5- Moses was between Aaron and Hur, and Christ was crucified between two thieves.
6- Moses by his prayer was an intercessor for his people before God, and Christ is the only atoning Intercessor for the sins of His people.

When Moses grew tired from much prayer, they seated him on a stone, and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on each side. This confirms the importance of perseverance in prayer and also the importance of the work of every individual in the Church, for without Hur and Aaron the victory would not have been accomplished, and not only without Moses.
In the end Israel's victory over Amalek was accomplished, so the enemies were afraid, and Israel continued on its way in the wilderness of Sinai.

God asked Moses to write down this victory in a book so that Israel would always remember God's supporting power. And He stressed to Joshua the importance of this victory, because God knows that Joshua will be the leader after Moses, so that He might encourage the people not to fear the strong inhabitants of the land of Canaan when they enter it. Amalek signifies Satan, so God promised his defeat and destruction, so that His people would not fear the enemy demons, however strong, and to declare the punishment of the wicked who persist in their evil, who must perish like Amalek.
Remember God's promises, and do not be disturbed by the threats of the enemies and their strength.

Moses expressed his thanks to God by building an altar and offering sacrifices to God upon it, and he called it "Jehovahnissi," that is, God is my banner and my standard, because he had triumphed and the name of God was exalted over Amalek and over all the enemies.
"The hand": the hand of Amalek.
"The throne of the Lord": the people of Israel.

Because Amalek attacked the people of God, he attacked God Himself, therefore God rose up against him in a war that lasted many years until Amalek perished in the days of David. Who can stand before God?!
Do not disobey God or defy Him with your sins lest He be angry with you, and do not persist in them lest they destroy you, and if you sin, hasten to repentance.
Jethro's visit and advice to Moses

Zipporah and her two sons went out with Moses to the land of Egypt, and she lived through the events of the ten plagues and then crossed the Red Sea with him. In the wilderness of Sinai it seems that she hastened to her father to bring him the good news of God's work with the children of Israel.
Jethro took his daughter Zipporah and his grandsons Gershom and Eliezer and set out to visit Moses and congratulate him on God's work with him.
Gershom: its meaning is stranger, because Moses was a stranger and sojourner in Egypt.

Eliezer: its meaning is God helps and has mercy, because God delivered Moses from the hand of Pharaoh on account of his killing the Egyptian man (ch. 2). Moses may have named his sons these names by the spirit of prophecy, because he knew the work of God that would happen with him.
Jethro sent word by one of those working for Moses and told him of his arrival with Moses' wife and sons.

Moses went out with joy to receive his father-in-law, and so did his wife and sons, and his humility appears in that he bowed down to his father-in-law out of respect for him and esteem for his age, although he was a priest of idols. Perhaps this humility and love are what influenced Jethro, in addition to his hearing of God's work with him, so he glorified God and offered sacrifices to Him (v. 12).
Offer your love with humility to all, near and far, and you will win them and their hearts will open to the love of God.
Moses sat with his father-in-law and told him in detail of God's works with His people, which Jethro had heard about briefly before, and these matters include:
1- How God delivered His people and brought them out of the land of Egypt by means of the ten plagues.

2- After they went out of Egypt, when Pharaoh pursued them to bring them back, and how God rescued them from his hand by means of the pillar of cloud or fire and the parting of the Red Sea, and then Pharaoh and his army were drowned in the sea.

3- How He rescued them from thirst on the way in the wilderness by turning the bitter water into sweet and bringing water out of the rock, and then rescued them from hunger by the manna and the quails.
God's works were great, so Jethro rejoiced in them and blessed God and glorified Him for rescuing His people from the hand of the mightiest of peoples at that time, the Egyptians.

In his glorifying God he exalted Him above all the pagan gods whom he worshipped, because His power, which appeared with Pharaoh and in the parting of the Red Sea, has no equal in the works of the pagan gods.

Continuing in glorifying God, Jethro offered sacrifices to Him. And when Aaron, Moses' brother, and the elders of Israel learned of the coming of Moses' father-in-law to visit him, they came to welcome him and ate with him, rejoicing in God's work and showing their love for Jethro and Moses.
Take care to thank God for all His works with you, and express your thanks by holy worship, works of goodness and service that you offer to others.

entries.section: (3) The problem of crowding at the judging

paragraphs.text: Moses was accustomed to set aside days for judging the people in their problems, and the next day was set aside for that, so many people came, and Moses sat judging their problems from morning until evening, which was of course exhausting for him, in addition to the people's weariness from the long waiting.

entries.section: (3) The problem of crowding at the judging

paragraphs.text: Jethro was amazed at the crowding of all the people with all their problems upon one person, Moses, to judge between them.

entries.section: (3) The problem of crowding at the judging

paragraphs.text: Moses told Jethro that the people meet problems in their dealings and that he knows the law of God and so guides them and judges between them. From this appears:
1- Moses' care, as a shepherd, for the problems of his people.
2- Settling disputes among them.
3- Teaching them God's judgments.
4- He was a mediator between the people and God.
And God equipped him with wisdom and gave him bodily strength to bear these burdens despite his advanced age, for he was past eighty.

It is good to seek God's guidance in all the details of your life through prayer, the Holy Bible and the guidance of the father of confession, and trust that if you seek it He will guide you, and you will walk reassured, rejoicing in your walk with Him.
Jethro drew Moses' attention to the difficulty of the present situation, for two reasons:
1- Moses' great exhaustion in judging all the people.
2- The people's weariness from the long waiting.

He advised him to divide the work, so that Moses would devote himself to prayer and seeking God's counsel for the great cases, and would guide the people with the general rules and commandments so that they might please God.

He asked him to appoint assistants to lead the people, making some of them rulers of thousands, and each of them is helped by rulers of hundreds, and these are helped by rulers of fifties, and finally each of the rulers of fifties is helped by rulers of tens. In all the assistants the following is required:
1- That they fear God and so hold to His commandments.
2- Faithful and careful in their work.
3- Not lovers of money and bribery, so that they are not influenced by the gifts of the wicked but please God and their conscience.
These assistants judge the small cases, while the great cases are referred to Moses himself.
"And God command thee so": God approves this counsel after you pray to Him.

In the end he told him that this counsel fulfills the carrying out of God's commandments and gives rest to him and to the people, so that they return to their dwellings at rest after their problems are solved.
Organizing every work and dividing it makes its execution easier, for wisdom is necessary in management, so take care to manage your life and organize everything.
Moses' humility appears in his obeying his father-in-law's counsel, for he is ready to learn from everyone, even the pagans, hearing the voice of God in every way that reaches him.
Moses chose assistants for himself and distributed the work among them, and reserved for himself only the great cases, as his father-in-law had advised him.
After Jethro had spent a period visiting Moses and was reassured about him, he returned to his country, Midian.
Be humble and learn from everyone, and you will hear the voice of God and advance in your life at all times. God speaks to you in many forms, and if you are humble you can hear.
Preparation for receiving the Ten Commandments

entries.section: (1) The time and place of receiving the commandments

paragraphs.text: The time for receiving the commandments from God was in the third month after the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt. They had to pass through the barren wilderness, almost dying of thirst and hunger, and then God satisfied them with manna and water, which signify Christ, and in the third month, which signifies the Resurrection, they receive the commandment, just as Christ passed through death and rose on the third day.

entries.section: (1) The time and place of receiving the commandments

paragraphs.text: It specifies that the place of receiving the commandments was in the wilderness of Sinai, in a wide valley with a great mountain before them, which it calls Mount Sinai, one of the known mountains in the wilderness of Sinai. They had moved from Rephidim, which is in the middle of the wilderness of Sinai toward the south, to the wilderness of Sinai, by which is meant the Sinai peninsula, that is, they moved a little toward the southeast (maps 1, 2). When man is stripped of the comfort of Egypt, that is, the comfort of the body and the pleasures of sin, he can in the barren wilderness hear the voice of God and enjoy His commandments.
Control your desires and do not give your body everything it asks, and your spirit will be refreshed and long for reading and prayer.

Moses was accustomed to speaking with God, so God called him from the mountain to come up to Him, and he went up to speak with Him. The people would not hear this voice, for it was for Moses alone, since he had a high spiritual rank in which he deserved to hear the voice of God.

In proportion to your longing for God, He lets you hear His voice, draws you near to Him, leads your life and gives you the joy of fellowship with Him. So take care to pray, that you may know God and hear Him.

God reminded Moses how He had rescued them from the mighty Egyptians and brought them out of the bondage of Egypt with a strong arm into the wilderness, and because of their faith in Him He lifted them up to Himself, to heaven, as an eagle seizes its prey and rises with it on high.

The eagles signify the Holy Spirit, who lifts us up to the heavenly things by faith and saves us from all dangers. Here appears the tenderness of God, who speaks with fatherhood, carrying His children like a little child, drawing them near to Him and rescuing them from the hands of the wicked.

God declared to Moses that if the people kept His commandments, which He would declare to them by Moses, He would grant them a special boldness, in that they would be a people distinguished for Him by His care, more than the rest of the peoples of the earth, which are all subject to God because He is the Creator of all.
Your care to carry out God's commandments gives you the joy of sonship to Him and of His care, for God is rich and gives to all who take refuge in Him, and distinguishes those who cling to Him.

In addition to His special care for them, God promises His people to give them the priesthood by which they draw near to Him through the sacrifices and all the rites, and He also promises them that they will be holy to Him, that is, set apart by His dwelling among them.

What is meant by "a kingdom of priests" is that there are priests in it, and here the special priesthood begins for the first time in the person of Aaron and his sons, for the head of the family used to be its priest before.
All these words God commanded Moses to declare to the people, so that, rejoicing in these promises, they might prepare to receive the commandments.
Moses gathered the elders of the children of Israel and declared to them everything God had said to him, so that they might know the word of God and teach it to the rest of the people.

The elders informed the people of God's words to Moses, and they rejoiced in His promises and declared their submission to God, and they came and told Moses so, although sadly they later turned back and left God when they worshipped the golden calf and when they murmured.
Do not be content with general promises to God, or with reading and hearing His voice in spiritual sermons, but would that you would strive to apply the word in your life.

When the people declared their submission and readiness to obey God's commandments, the Lord rejoiced in them and promised Moses to appear to all the people in a thick cloud, in dense fog. This declares the greatness of God and the inability of any human being to comprehend all that is in Him.

God asked Moses to prepare the people to see Him, by bodily purification, that is, the washing of their bodies today and the day after, as a symbol of inner purity, and the washing of clothes for the same purpose, and also by abstaining from bodily relations between husband and wife; their sanctification, that is, setting themselves apart for God and His worship, as they prepare to meet God. This also happens in the New Testament when husband and wife abstain from bodily relations before Communion.
Here is a confirmation of the idea of the Resurrection through the third day, in which God appears and gives His commandments while they have been purified for three days.
"Bounds": by setting marks such as pillars of stones or pits or any marks that the people may not pass around the holy mountain.

When God comes down upon the mountain, all of it becomes holy, like the altar in the temple of the New Testament, upon which God descends with His Body and Blood. Therefore He asked Moses to warn the people not to approach the mountain, and any man or beast that touches the mountain is put to death. This shows the holiness of God and that there must be no laxity in approaching Him, by repentance and confession before Communion. It also signifies spiritually the necessity of man's ridding himself of the sins of emotional attachment that hinder him from God, signified by the man who is put to death, and likewise the animal lusts, signified by the killing of the animal.

And when they hear the sound of the trumpet, which is either a sound coming from God or Moses commands one of his helpers to blow the trumpet, then those whom God chose, who are mentioned in (ch. 24), come forward to approach the mountain, and they are Moses, Aaron and his sons, and the seventy elders.

Moses instructed the people how to prepare, by washing their clothes and abstaining from marital relations, and the people obeyed. This is a clear teaching of the importance of chastity in married life when drawing near to God by partaking of the Holy Sacraments.

entries.section: (4) The appearance of God on the mountain

paragraphs.text: At the time God had appointed, that is, after the people had been purified for three days, God appeared with the following:
1- Thunders: loud sounds that declare the power of God.
2- Lightnings: shining with brilliance, declaring the glory and splendor of God.

3- A cloud: it signifies the presence of God, as happened at the Transfiguration, for it is white, dense and high in the heavens, so it declares the glory of God and also His depths, which no one knows.
4- A trumpet: a loud sound to warn people for striving and war, meaning the feeling of the fear of God and readiness for Him.
And before the greatness of God the people were very afraid and trembled at His majesty.
The fear of God makes you keep away from every sin and enjoy fellowship with Him, and you no longer fear anything earthly.

entries.section: (4) The appearance of God on the mountain

paragraphs.text: Moses brought the people out of their tents inside the camp and stood them before the mountain, and they were in great fear because of the appearance of God.

entries.section: (4) The appearance of God on the mountain

paragraphs.text: The fifth appearance of God was in the form of a great fire on the top of the mountain, which gave off thick smoke, for our God is a consuming fire that consumes all the evil in us if we repent, and torments us forever if we refuse it. And the mountain shook like one trembling before the fire, the fog, the thunders and the lightnings.

entries.section: (4) The appearance of God on the mountain

paragraphs.text: The sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder to declare the presence of God, and in the midst of these manifestations God began to speak with Moses.

entries.section: (5) A warning to the people and the priests

paragraphs.text: God called Moses in the midst of these powerful manifestations to go up to the mountain, and he obeyed and went up.

entries.section: (5) A warning to the people and the priests

paragraphs.text: God was concerned for His people, so He stressed to Moses to go down and warn the people for the second time not to approach the mountain and touch it, lest they die.
Here God appears with great fear in the Old Testament, while in the New Testament, besides the fear of Him, He has given His people to gather around Him with boldness and love.

entries.section: (5) A warning to the people and the priests

paragraphs.text: The sanctification included the priests also, by whom is meant the heads of the clans and families, because the priesthood had not yet been declared by God's choosing Aaron and his sons. What is meant is the care of all the people and their heads to purify themselves, indeed the heads are the more responsible, as an example to the people, to purify themselves.
Take care for the purity of your heart, if you are a father or a servant, to be an example for those whom you raise or teach, so that you gain the salvation of your soul and of others.

entries.section: (5) A warning to the people and the priests

paragraphs.text: Moses answered God that he had already declared to the people the divine warning not to approach the mountain lest they die, but God in His fatherhood, and because He knows the laxity and weakness of His children, commanded him to go down and warn them for the second time so that none of them should die, and Moses obeyed and went down and warned the people again.
The Ten Commandments
After Moses went up and entered the thick fog alone, the Lord spoke with him and gave him the Ten Commandments. The following is noticed in the commandments:

1- Their number is ten, which signifies perfection, that is, the perfection of teaching and guidance, like the ten virgins in the parable of the ten virgins (Mt 25:1-3) and the ten pieces of silver in the parable of the lost piece of silver (Lk 15:8, 9), as God also asks for tithes.
2- The division of the commandments:

a- The first four concern the relation with God, taking the first commandment to be the worship of the one God and the second commandment to be not worshipping images, while the six commandments that follow concern the relation with others.

b- There is another division that combines the first and second commandments, so the commandments concerning God are three, and separates the coveting of the neighbor's wife in the tenth commandment from the coveting of his possessions, so the commandments concerning the relation with others become seven.

c- The commandments were written on two tablets of stone, so some explain that the first five were written together, and in this way the commandment to honor parents is joined to the relation with God, and this is an exaltation of the fifth commandment.

3- Man's inability: these commandments are negative except the fourth and the fifth, and they reveal man's inability and his sins, but by the grace of the Holy Spirit in the New Testament he is able to carry them out.

4- Christ fulfills the commandments: Christ showed the causes of sin, such as anger, which is the origin of murder, and the look, the origin of adultery; so He confirms the commandments because they are His word, and fulfills them.
5- A summary of the commandments: Christ summed them up in two commandments, which are:
a- Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.
b- Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself). Lk 10:27)

6- The time of the giving of the commandments: fifty days after the first Passover that was kept in Egypt. After the fourteenth day of the first month to the end of the second month is 45 days, to which is added the day of Moses' going up the mountain and the day of his return to the people, in addition to their sanctification for three days, so the total is fifty days, and this signifies the descent of the Holy Spirit and His sanctification of the Church on the fiftieth day.

The first commandment declares the oneness of God and forbids the worship of the gods of the pagan nations surrounding the children of Israel, and these gods appear today in the form of the material things of the world, its positions and all its lusts. The children of Israel fell into the worship of pagan gods and sometimes mixed the worship of God with idols, as when they made the golden calf or the calves that Jeroboam set up, as we mix our spiritual life today with the ideas of the world.

The second commandment forbids the making of statues and images of the pagan gods for the purpose of worshipping them, since the making of statues and images of the pagan gods was widespread in the Old Testament. But the use of icons to recall the life of Christ and the saints helps fervent worship. The Orthodox Church prefers the use of icons and not the use of statues like the Catholic Church, because statues give the meaning bodily form and so are more influential, and may draw some to cling to them, such as making statues of the saints, and it is feared that they may distract people from the worship of God, especially if they are statues made with precision and beauty.

And God forbids the making of statues and images of the pagan gods because He loves us with the love of a bridegroom for his bride and is jealous over us if we leave Him and are occupied with idols or the material things of the world.

God's visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children does not mean that the fathers sin and the innocent children are punished, because in Ezekiel and Jeremiah God utterly rejects this saying when He says, "Ye shall no more use this proverb: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge" (Jer 31:29, 30; Ezek 18:1-25). What is meant is that if the children persist in the errors of their fathers to the third and fourth generation, God punishes them for their clinging to their fathers' errors. It shows God's longsuffering, in that He gives man life to the third and fourth generation that perhaps he may repent, but every person, whether of the fathers or the children, is responsible for his own error and is repaid for it. So He visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, that is, He disciplines them and punishes them in the third and fourth generation because they walked in the sins of their fathers; the fathers are responsible for their sins and for their causing their children to stumble, and the children are responsible for their disobedience to God and their persisting in the sins of their fathers. But if the children obey God and reject the sins of their fathers, they become children blessed by God. At the same time God blesses those who love Him, who hold to His worship and the carrying out of His commandments. It is noticed that the blessing for the obedient is greater than the punishment for those who persist in the evils of their fathers, for He says that the discipline is to the third and fourth generation, while the blessing is to thousands.

The third commandment: God wanted to keep His people from uttering the names of the gods of the pagan nations and having recourse to them, so He allowed them to utter His name in all their dealings, but not falsely and in vain or without need, and they are not to utter it with mockery and recklessness or with hypocrisy, because His name is great and holy. In the New Testament we do not swear by it at all in our material dealings, since we have matured spiritually and believe that He is the only God, and we mention it only for sanctification in our prayers (Mt 5:33-37).

The fourth commandment: this is the sanctification of the seventh day, because on it God finished the creation of the whole world and rested and was pleased with what He had made; therefore, in glorification of God, He commanded them to sanctify the seventh day, the Sabbath, so that they do no material work on it but devote it to worship, all the people and the slaves also. In the New Testament, God has completed His work in our salvation by the Resurrection, and the glory of Sunday surpassed that of the Sabbath: Christ appeared to His disciples on Sunday, the Holy Spirit descended on Sunday, and since the apostolic age they gathered on Sunday to partake of the Holy Sacraments (Acts 20:7). Therefore the Lord's Day in the New Testament is Sunday, in addition to the continued honoring of the Sabbath also because God completed the creation of the world in it, so there is no fasting without eating on it as on Sunday, except the Saturday of the Light, to remember Christ's being in the tomb.
The Jews kept the Sabbath day for the following:
1- Offering greater worship, by doubling the morning and evening burnt offering.
2- Abstaining from material works, including kindling a fire.

3- Permitting a few necessary works such as loosing the animals and watering them and rescuing them if they fell into a pit (Deut 12:11), and moving a limited distance called a Sabbath day's journey, which is about a mile.
4- Being an opportunity for rest for their bodies and their slaves (Deut 5:14, 15).
5- Forbidding going out to gather the manna, because it does not fall on this day.
6- They were allowed to cook food.
7- Besides their worship, they took care to do good.

But the elders of the Jews erred through the ages in the sanctification of the Sabbath day: they concerned themselves with not working and set many limits for it, and neglected doing good and worship, as appeared in their opposition to the miracles of Christ on the Sabbath (Jn 5:9). As for the believers in the Church of the New Testament, they honor Sunday by the following:
1- Freeing themselves from material work as far as possible.
2- Attending the Divine Liturgy as much as they can, if their work does not prevent them.
3- Increasing worship, in prayers and readings.
4- Examining the soul, repentance and meditation on God's mercies and love in quiet solitude.
5- Attending spiritual meetings if possible.
6- Visiting the brethren and those who are far away, to bind them to the Church.
7- Works of goodness such as helping the needy and visiting the sick, the orphans and the weak of every kind.

The fifth commandment: because of the parents' toil and their true love, which appears in the raising of their children, God asked the children to honor their parents, not only with kind words and respect but also with obedience, and likewise to provide for their needs when they advance in age and the children become able to help them. This is the only commandment connected with a divine promise, which is length of days upon the earth. What is meant is days filled with peace on earth by God's blessing, and it also signifies the new earth in the Kingdom, where it lasts forever in rest with God. So the meaning of length of days is:
1- Length of the days of life on earth in some cases, for doing good and worship, so that one is a light to others.
2- The abundance of days that a person lives with God, even if his life is short.
3- The extension of the days that a person lives spiritually in the Kingdom of Heaven, that is, the new earth that God grants to whoever obeys His commandments.

And in the New Testament God confirms this commandment by Christ's submission to the Virgin and Joseph the carpenter (Lk 3:51) and His obedience to her at the wedding in Cana of Galilee and His working the first miracle in honor of her (Jn 2) and His care for her on the Cross by charging John to take care of her (Jn 19:26, 27). The New Testament also placed one reservation, which is that their obedience be in the Lord, that is, not contrary to His commandments. And Christ was angry with the priests of the Jews who distorted this important commandment by replacing it with offerings on behalf of the parents and neglecting their support by their children (Mt 15:4-6).

The sixth commandment: God greatly values the human soul and declares His displeasure at the shedding of blood, as He was displeased with Cain when he killed Abel (Gen 4:8). And if God commanded the killing of the murderer and the adulterer, this was to declare His hatred of sin; but in the New Testament, after spiritual maturity, God hates sin but loves the sinner and is longsuffering toward him that perhaps he may repent.
And the sin of murder has many kinds, such as:
1- A man's killing his brother deliberately by any means.
2- A man's killing himself by suicide.
3- Endangering the life of another unintentionally but through negligence, such as housing them in houses about to collapse or not making a parapet for the stairs or the roof (Deut 22:8).
4- Letting loose animals that can kill a person, such as the goring ox (Ex 21:28-32).
5- Putting out poisonous substances without declaring it, so that they kill whoever drinks or eats them without knowing.
6- Drinking wine in large quantities, which can kill a person or hasten his death.
7- Excessive exhaustion of the body.
8- Persisting in fornication to the point of severe exhaustion.
But killing is permitted in certain cases, which are:
1- Self-defense.
2- Soldiers in war, in obedience to the authorities (Rom 13:4).
3- The authorities' putting to death criminals who harm others.
And in the New Testament Christ forbade not only killing but also its first causes, which is anger (Mt 5:21, 22).

The seventh commandment: adultery is a great sin in which man sins against God and also against his own body, and it is called uncleanness; by it man defiles himself and the other with whom he committed adultery, and defiles the clothes, the place and the whole land. And in the New Testament Christ warned of the cause of its beginning, which is the evil look, and counted it adultery so that the chaste person might keep away from it (Mt 5:28). Thus Christ rejected every form of adultery such as:
1- Evil sights in the streets and in the media.
2- Women's causing others to stumble by immodest clothing that attracts attention, and by glances and smiles and all means of attracting attention, with the kinds of stumbling fashion.
3- Infatuation and emotional attachment.
4- Unclean thoughts.
5- Stumbling words and conversations.
6- Reading stumbling books.
7- Leniency in joking and the use of the hands.
8- Slipping into the steps of complete adultery.
9- Sexual perversion.
10- A person's arousing himself bodily.

The eighth commandment: theft is a shameful thing that appeared from the beginning of creation, before the giving of the Ten Commandments, when man took what was not his. The first sin was a theft, because it was an eating from the tree from which God had forbidden man to eat, and Laban's accusing Jacob of stealing his idols, and likewise Joseph's accusing his brothers of stealing his cup, was considered a shameful matter deserving the arrest and trial of whoever did it.

Theft includes any possessions of another, or even his ideas, and not paying tithes is robbing God. Theft is considered more shameful when it is the plundering of the needy such as the widow and the orphan, or the theft of sacred things. The New Testament called the thief to leave this evil and come out of his selfishness by working to meet his own needs and even to give to the needy (Eph 4:28).

The ninth commandment: false witness is lying, and its danger lies in changing the facts, and therefore God hates it, because it acquits the guilty and condemns the innocent and stirs up quarrels among people. It is the work of Satan, who is described as a liar and the father of lies, and therefore the Law provides that testimony be on the mouth of two or three witnesses, to avoid lying as far as possible (Deut 19:15).

The tenth commandment: it forbids covetousness and the desiring of what belongs to another, and so it shows the cause of the previous sins, which is the desire of the heart before the deed that the previous commandments forbid. The commandment includes two matters:
1- The neighbor's wife, in which, if a person persists, he falls into adultery.
2- The possessions of another, in which, if a person persists, he falls into theft or murder.
And the New Testament has given us the ability to carry out this commandment by the grace of the Holy Spirit.

Let God's commandments be before your eyes so that they light your way and keep you from sin; do not be lax and be carried along with the current of the evil world, and if you sin by breaking any commandment, hasten to repentance, and if you find it difficult to carry out in any situation, ask God's help to make it easy for you to carry it out, and so you will receive God's pleasure and blessings and keep your peace.

Before the fearful sight of God on the mountain with fire, thunders, lightnings, fog and trumpet, the people were very afraid, so they asked Moses to speak himself with God on the mountain and then come to them in the camp and teach them what God commands.

Moses explained to the people the reason for these powerful manifestations that accompanied the appearance of God, which was the testing of the people, that is, fixing the fear of God in their hearts so that they would obey His commandments and not sin against Him by worshipping idols or walking in the evils of the nations.
The people stood far from the holy mountain, near their tents, while Moses went up the mountain in the midst of the fog to speak with God.

It is good to feel the fear of God so that you reject sin and the semblance of sin, that is, all its causes, even if they seem small, because sin is a defiance of God and a disobedience of His commands and deserves death.

entries.section: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: God declared to Moses commandments for him to teach to the people, the first of which is that He dwells in heaven, that is, higher than everything they see on earth, and His loftiness above all the pagan gods has appeared in the thunders, lightnings, fire... etc., so that they might worship Him, confident of His power, and reject the idols.

entries.section: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: He forbade them to make statues, whether of the pagan gods or even for His worship, as they made the golden calf, and not to resemble the nations in making them of silver and gold with their material glitter, because God dwells in heaven and is higher than all material things. It is noticed that they possessed gold and silver from what they had taken from their neighbors in Egypt.

entries.section: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: "In all places where I record my name": every place in which God declares His glory by speaking with His pious ones or in any heavenly appearances.

He commanded the people to offer sacrifices to God on altars made of earth, that is, mud brick, so that their concentration would be on the sacrifice and on pleasing God and not on the form of the altar, and then God blesses them from heaven. These altars suited their wandering in the wilderness or in any other places afterward.

entries.section: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: Altars may be made of stones, but they are joined to one another with earth and set as they are without carving, so that they do not carve on them shapes like the pagan idols and so turn to the worship of idols through the making of altars.

entries.section: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

paragraphs.text: He also commanded them to make the altars directly on the ground and not raised so that they would reach them by steps. The reason is that their nakedness not be uncovered, and what is meant even more than this is their humility, so that the shame of their pride may not be uncovered, and so that they would not resemble the pagans, who built their altars on high places. But afterward they were permitted to make steps, as in Solomon's temple (2 Chr 4:1) and in the days of the prophet Ezekiel (Ezek 43:17).

Would that you would be humble when you pray, whether in the church or in the closet, for then your prayer is accepted. And let your concentration be on the sense of God and not on the form of the words or the melodies.
The slave, killing and striking in the Law
Judgments: laws that God set down in His high wisdom.

God gave Moses not only the Ten Commandments but a law, or Law, covering people's conduct in various respects, and the first thing it speaks of in the Law is servants, because this system prevailed in the world at that time. The Law provides that the Hebrew servant be treated with love, for he is a servant for a temporary period of six years at most, and in the seventh year he is set free.

The number (7) signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who convicts us of every sin and forgives it for us and so frees us from it. This law declares that the servant is not owned like a piece of furniture or an animal but is so for a temporary period, in order to change the idea of enslavement within man and free him from it, and on the other hand it eases the lot of the servants who have been sold to their masters because of poverty.
It also confirms the value of faith, for this law applies to the Hebrew only, to declare that faith frees us from bondage.

The Law also provides for respect for the servant's property: if he was married before his servitude, then when he is set free he takes his wife with him; but if his master had given him one of the maidservants to marry and he had children by her, he goes out alone and leaves his wife and children, because they are not his own but his master's. So this law declares the importance of respecting the property of others and of not exploiting opportunities to control others.
"The judges": what is meant is the judges who sit near the gate of the city and judge by the law of God.

If the servant chooses of his own will to remain with his wife and children because of his emotional attachment to them and his comfort in serving his master, he remains a servant all his life with this master. Here this matter must be declared before the whole city, that is, before the judges or elders of the city who sit in its square at its entrance, and he brings him to the gate of the city before all those entering and going out, or to the door post of the city gate (the side of the door), and bores his ear through, so that it will be a visible sign before the people, in order to protect the servant who did not wish to continue in his master's servitude, so that his master may not come and say that this servant of mine agreed to be with me all his life when this has not actually happened, since they will not find a hole in his ear. He chose the ear as a conspicuous organ in man, concerned with hearing, that is, to declare his readiness to obey his master all his life.

And the servant's choosing to remain with his master all his life is a reference to the spiritual man's accepting, in the New Testament, to be a servant of Christ, who bought him with His blood, in order to enjoy God's care and fellowship with his fellow believers (his wife and children), or for the sanctification of his body and his senses, which the wife and children signify.

If a Hebrew man becomes poor and sells his daughter as a maidservant and her master marries her, she does not go out after the period of servitude has ended, but remains a free wife with her master, who has become her husband, and lives with him as a free woman. But if she was merely a maidservant and not a wife, she goes out in the seventh year or the year of jubilee and is freed. Thus, when she leaves her father's house for her master, she is honored as a servant in the house and not a slave, because she stays with her master for a period until her father or her kin are able to redeem her and pay her price, or she is let go free in the seventh year and returns with honor to her father's house.

If a master marries his maidservant and then wants to divorce her, he cannot sell her to anyone but is bound to care for her and provide for her, because he has taken pleasure in marrying her; this marriage must be respected, for it is not merely a pleasure or a personal benefit.

Here appears respect for marriage even before Christianity declared it a holy sacrament, and also the husband's responsibility for his wife, even if she was a maidservant, so that he cares for her and her feelings, for she is not an instrument of pleasure as the Gentiles treat her. That is, if he wants to separate from her and divorce her, he frees her to marry a Hebrew man and not a Gentile, and he also does not sell her to a Gentile man, because he took pleasure in living with her, so he has no right to sell her as a maidservant, since he did not keep her as a mere maidservant.

Among the rights of the maidservant whom the master marries to his son is that he give her her dowry of jewels or possessions and hold a wedding celebration for her like the other girls who are not maidservants.

Here is a confirmation of respect for the servant's property and also esteem for her feelings, for the dowry or the betrothal gift is a proof of the husband's love for his wife. But if the maidservant lived with her master's son and was set free in the seventh year, she lives after that as an honored wife and not a maidservant, and if he divorces her she is treated as a free woman and takes all her possessions.

If the master wants to marry another woman, he is bound to take care of his first wife in providing for her and in his bodily union with her, but if he refuses, he frees her. Here we see that although custom and the Law permitted a plurality of wives, they respected the first marriage even if it was to a maidservant, and if the husband neglected his responsibility for his wife, he frees her as a punishment to him for his neglect, that is, he does not sell her to anyone. We notice from (Neh 5:5-8) that after the captivity the bondage of the Hebrews to one another was abolished.

Would that you would feel your responsibility toward those around you and give them their rights before you demand duties of them, and if you wrong them, you should apologize and compensate them for any harm that resulted from your wronging them.

The life of man is the most precious thing, therefore whoever despises it is punished with a like punishment, so whoever kills deliberately must be put to death. The Law teaches the importance of respecting the lives of others and of not wronging them, whether bodily, psychologically or spiritually, as Christianity explained in more detail (Mt 5:21-26).

Whoever kills another by accident, "God deliver him into his hand," is not put to death, because he did not intend to kill him, and God appointed cities to which this killer may flee (the cities of refuge), which God determined to Moses and Joshua carried out (Num 35:6-15; Josh 20); they signify Christ, to whom we take refuge, and He protects us and removes from us the punishment of our sins. This killer is sufficiently punished by being deprived of his family, his possessions and his work, and this is a temporary punishment until the great priest dies or the year of jubilee, that is, the fiftieth, comes, and he is freed and no one can take revenge on him. The death of the great priest signifies the death of Christ, who frees us from the bondage of sin.
This sin is a sin of laxity, so it has a punishment, but not like the punishment of murder.
"The altar of God" means the bronze altar on which the burnt offerings are offered in the tabernacle of the congregation, the details of whose construction God will give to Moses after this speech.

And the altar represents the presence of God among His people and His keeping and rescuing them from every danger, because upon it is the sacrifice that signifies the Redeemer and Savior. If a man kills another deliberately he must be put to death, because he despised his brother's life, as mentioned in (v. 12), and even if he hastens to the altar and clings to it, he is taken and put to death, because the one who killed his brother unintentionally would take refuge at the altar until the judges examined him, and if that was established he would go to the cities of refuge, but if it was deliberate he must be put to death, as happened in the days of Solomon when Joab clung to the horns of the altar (1 Kgs 2:28-32).

It moves to another law besides killing, which is striking, and begins with a son's striking his father or his mother; for the sake of their great honor, as the fifth commandment states, this son must be put to death. From here is understood the confirmation of honoring parents and respecting their feelings and not wronging them in any way, even if they err.
