Two boards are made for the two corners of the tabernacle, that is, at the back of the Holy of Holies, and they have a doubled thickness to secure the walls of the tabernacle, that is, the north, west and south walls.

And six boards are made for the back of the tabernacle, that is, its west wall, which is the wall of the Holy of Holies, each a cubit and a half wide, so that when they are set close together their width is 9 cubits and their height 10 cubits. In the two corners the two thick boards mentioned in (v. 23) are placed, and most likely the end of the ordinary board is fixed inside this thick board at the corner by means of a tongue and groove. In the same way the ends of the boards in the north wall and the south wall are fixed by tongue and groove into the two corner boards. The width of the two corner boards is not mentioned; it may be less, about 3/4 of a cubit, with a length of 10 cubits.

"One ring": this means the upper ring on the board, since each board has three gold rings through which the bars mentioned in (v. 26) pass. The two corner boards are each double, that is, thick, twice the thickness of the ordinary board from its bottom to its top, while the ring mentioned refers to gold rings, in which crosswise boards are fixed, as will be mentioned in (v. 26).

Thus the west wall of the tabernacle is made up of eight boards, six of which are each a cubit and a half wide and ten cubits high, while the two corner boards are of doubled thickness and their length is ten cubits, but their width may be half that of the ordinary board, that is, 3/4 of a cubit, so that part of them projects on the two sides of the tabernacle, so that the width of the west wall on the inside is ten cubits.
The boards signify the Apostles or the believers in the New Testament, who rely on the word of God in their faith, and the bases also signify the prophets of the Old Testament.
Be steadfast in the word of God and believe it however much the world opposes you, and you will be firmly established in the Church of God, enjoy His presence, and find your salvation and your peace.

To secure the boards of the tabernacle, they are fixed not only vertically in the ground but also crosswise to one another by means of crosswise boards fixed to them. These are five bars made of acacia wood, placed on three levels (fig. 9:)

1- Two bars are placed on the upper level, on one horizontal level, each fixed in ten boards by means of gold rings fixed in each board, and the bars are overlaid with gold. They signify Christ, God incarnate, for gold refers to divinity and acacia wood to humanity.
2- The lower level of the bars, like the upper, consists of two bars, each fixed in ten boards, and the two are also on one horizontal level.

3- The third bar is fixed in the middle of the boards, that is, at a height of 5 cubits, and it is a long bar fixed in the twenty boards by means of rings fixed in each board and made of gold. This bar is also overlaid with gold and is parallel to the upper and lower bars and placed between them. Two bars. Rings made of gold. 30 cubits. Bars made of acacia wood. Cubits. Overlaid with gold. A long bar in the middle. (a) Bars for the north and south walls of the tabernacle. 10 cubits. Cubits. (b) Bars for the west wall of the tabernacle. Figure (9:) The bars of the tabernacle

Bars are made for the north wall of the tabernacle just as for the south, in the same form, and the west wall likewise has bars made for it on three levels and in the same form, but their length is shorter than the bars of the north or south walls, because this wall is ten cubits long, while the north and south walls are each 30 cubits long.

"From end to end" means from the first board to board number 20, that is, along the length of the south wall or along the length of the north wall, but on the upper and lower levels there are on each two bars on one horizontal level instead of one bar.

The bars are overlaid with gold and the rings are made into houses for them of gold, which signifies heaven and the presence of God, or divinity. Whoever enters the tent sees it: he sees wooden walls with golden bars fixed by golden rings.
Moses saw all these details with his own eyes for a long time during the forty days that he spent with God, and He may have given him specific drawings for all parts of the tent.

Be careful in your life to be firm in God through the means of grace, which are represented by the silver bases and the gilded wooden bars, which secure your senses and all your abilities in the spiritual life and nurture your faith, which is signified by the wooden boards.

The veil is a curtain that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies and is made of linen (fine twined linen), embroidered and adorned with cloth of blue, purple and scarlet, with two angels of the order of the Cherubim drawn on it. The veil proclaims the existence of a barrier between God and man, which is sin, and which would be removed by the death of Christ when the veil of the Temple was torn. As for the curtain before the sanctuary of the New Testament, it is merely a proclamation of the sanctity of the sanctuary, but it is opened throughout the Liturgy so that the believers may see everything and even partake of the Body and Blood of Christ (figs. 6, 10, 11).
Gold rings. Two angels of the order of the Cherubim. 4 pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Silver bases. Figure (10:) The veil with its pillars

God asked Moses to set up four pillars of acacia wood. Their width and thickness are not specified, but they are probably like the rest of the boards. He overlays them with gold, and they rest on a base of silver sunk into the ground, and they have hooks at their top, that is, gold rings, on which to hang the veil.

The clasps are the golden threads that join the two couplings, and the place where the two pieces meet is directly above the veil. Thus the veil screens the Holy of Holies, in which the ark of the covenant is placed, so that no one sees it except the high priest once a year, bringing with him the blood of animals, as a reference to the blood of Christ, who takes us through the veil and overcomes sin after having paid its debt by death.
The ark of the testimony is covered with the cover on which are the two Cherubim.

He places the table of showbread in the Holy Place on the right of one entering the Holy Place and the lampstand on his left, so that the lampstand is on the south side and the table on the north side, that is, the north (fig. 11). The ark. The veil. The Holy of Holies. The altar of incense. The Holy Place. The table of showbread. The lampstand. The outer court. The golden. The laver. The altar of burnt offering. Aaron. Moses. Figure (11)

In front of the Holy Place a hanging is made, that is, a curtain of linen (fine twined linen), and he embroiders it with cloth of blue, purple and scarlet by a skilled tailor (embroiderer), who is Bezaleel (ch. 31:1) and his helpers (fig. 12). Hooks of gold. A curtain of linen. 5 pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Bronze bases. Figure (12:) The hanging and its pillars

The hanging is fixed on five pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with bronze bases, while their hooks, that is, their rings fixed at the top of the boards, are made of gold, so that the hanging may be hung on them, so that no one sees the entrance of the Holy Place except the priests, for it proclaims the dignity of the Holy Place.

It is noted that the hanging, that is, the entrance of the Holy Place, is hung on five boards for greater security, since the priests enter by it every day, while the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies is hung on four boards only, because the high priest enters by it once a year on the Day of Atonement. From what has preceded we see that the entrance of the Holy Place is covered from top to bottom by four cubits (the sixth curtain) (v. 9), therefore the hanging serves as a curtain hung on the pillars to cover the entrance of the Holy Place completely.
The hanging is at the entrance of the Holy Place on the east, as is the entrance of the tent, while the Holy of Holies is on the west, for the following reasons:
1- So that they would not share with the pagan nations that worship the sun and face toward the east.
2- It is beneficial for the rays of the sun to enter from the east in the morning to light the entrance of the tent and the outer court.
As for the Church in the New Testament, the sanctuary in it is toward the east and the entrance of the church is from the west, for the following reasons:
1- The first Paradise in which Adam was created was toward the east (Gen 2:8), and after our departure from this life we return to Paradise.
2- Christ was born in the east, that is, Bethlehem.
3- The star appeared to the Magi in the east (Mt 2:2).
4- Christ is the Sun of Righteousness, so the sun that rises points to Him.
5- Christ will come at His Second Coming like the lightning that comes out of the east (Mt 24:27).
May you enjoy the Body and Blood of the Lord and God's revelation of Himself in the New Testament, available to you in the Church. The bronze altar and the wall of the tabernacle

The altar is made of acacia wood, which signifies the wood of the Cross, and it is in the shape of a rectangular solid, that is, the shape of a tomb, as a symbol of the death of Christ, for on this altar were offered the sacrifices that signify the crucified Christ who died for us (fig. 13). The dimensions of the altar are five cubits in length and five cubits in width, as a symbol of the five senses of man, which are sanctified by Christ the Redeemer in their spiritual striving, and as a symbol of the five offerings mentioned in the Book of Leviticus, which point to the crucified Christ. Its height is three cubits, as a symbol of the risen Christ, for He died for us and then rose on the third day. And because the altar is high, they would mostly go up to it by an inclined surface, since God forbade them to go up to the altars by steps (ch. 20:25). Figure (13:) The altar of burnt offering (the bronze altar)

Four horns are made for the altar at its four corners, and these horns are made from one block of wood with the corner post, not a horn fixed to the post by mortising. The horn signifies strength, because the redemption of Christ is strong and takes away all the sins of the world. The sacrifices were bound to the horns of the altar until they were slaughtered. And the wronged person would hold fast to the horns of the altar, proclaiming his clinging to God to save him from injustice and death.
The altar is overlaid with bronze plates, and bronze signifies endurance and steadfastness, as Christ endured sufferings for us on the Cross.
The requisites and instruments of the altar are all made of bronze, and they are:-
1- Its pans: vessels in which the ashes of the burnt offerings are gathered to be cast outside the camp; the word is the plural of "pot," which may be used for cooking meat.
2- Its shovels: the plural of "shovel," a scoop (spade) for gathering the ashes from the altar.
3- Basins: the plural of "basin," a flat vessel like a washbowl, for gathering the blood of the slaughtered animals.
4- Fleshhooks: the plural of "fleshhook," a three-pronged fork with a long handle for lifting pieces of meat from the altar or those placed in the pots.

5- Firepans: the plural of "firepan," in which burning coals are placed; they may have been used to keep the holy fire while the ashes of the burnt offerings were removed or when the tent was moved from place to place (Lev 9:24).

A network grating surrounds the altar in its lower half, that is, to a height of a cubit and a half from the ground, so that the priests' feet cannot touch the altar when they approach to offer the sacrifices on it, out of respect for it, but touch only this network barrier made of bronze. At the top of this network barrier four rings are made at the corners of the altar, and these rings are made of bronze and fixed at its four corners, to put the two staves in them to carry the altar when moving camp.

A compass is made for the altar, surrounding it a little below its upper surface. It is most probably like a ledge around the altar, projecting 10-20 cm on all sides, so that if a piece of meat falls it falls on it and not on the ground.
He makes two staves of acacia wood and overlays them with bronze, which signifies the crucified Christ who endured sufferings for us.
The two staves are put into the bronze rings that are on the two sides of the altar.

The bronze altar consists of four walls and an upper top on which are the four horns, but it is hollow inside because it signifies the tomb. It is confirmed here that Moses saw all the details of the tent of meeting on the mountain in the form of pictures or models.

Endure sufferings for the sake of Christ, who endured sufferings for you and who is signified by this bronze altar, and do not murmur or compare yourself with others, but ask for God's help, and you will experience His fellowship, your will will be strengthened, and you will enjoy peace.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The court of the tabernacle: that is, the outer court surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, in which are the laver and the bronze altar.

It tells us about the outer wall of the tent of meeting, inside which is a courtyard with the tabernacle in its midst. The bronze altar is in the courtyard at the entrance of the tent, then the laver, and after that the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies (figs. 14, 15). The south wall, that is, the one on the side toward the south, is 100 cubits long and is made of linen hangings. Southward: that is, the south, which is the left of one entering by the east door of the tent.

100 cubits. The pillar of cloud and fire. North. 50 cubits. The laver. The altar of burnt offering. The tent of meeting. The outer court. Figure (14) The outer walls of the court of the tabernacle. (1) A pillar of bronze. (3) A hook of silver. (2) A curtain. (4) A rod of silver. (5) Pins. (6) A base of bronze. 15 cubits. 20 cubits. 15 cubits. A hanging of blue, purple, scarlet and linen. The outer gate or the east wall. Figure (15)

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The south wall is hung on 20 pillars made of bronze, and the hooks, that is, their upper rings on which the hangings are hung, are made of silver. These bronze pillars are joined by crosswise pillars, which are rods, most probably fixed through the silver hooks, so that the whole wall is fixed as one unit. The pillars are fixed in the ground and are then also secured by pins on the inside and outside, drawn by cords from the top of the pillar, to protect the wall from the wind. The bronze pillars are fixed in bronze bases in the ground, and there may also be pins for the tabernacle, to which cords are tied to secure it on its three sides, the north, the west and the south.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The north wall is exactly like the south wall, standing on 20 pillars joined by silver rods, with the linen hangings hung on the bronze pillars, and it is likewise fixed in the ground with bronze pins tied with cords on the inside and outside.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The west wall is 50 cubits wide. Its linen hangings are fixed on ten bronze pillars fixed in the ground with bronze bases, and its silver rods are fixed in the silver hooks in the pillars to join the pillars together. It also has bronze pins tying it with cords on the inside and outside.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The east wall consists of two parts of the wall, each 15 cubits, fixed on three bronze pillars in the same form as the rest of the wall and with the same hangings, so that there are two sides, right and left, on the east, each 15 cubits, and between them the main gate of the tent of meeting, 20 cubits wide, before which is the bronze altar, then the laver, and after that the tabernacle itself.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The east gate is a curtain of linen embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet, hung on four pillars like the previous pillars but without pins. Entry was by lifting the curtain and entering from under it or beside it. It is noted that the curtain of the gate is different from the hangings of the wall, for it is embroidered in the colors blue, purple and scarlet, because Christ is the door, and He is the King of kings (purple), the Redeemer (scarlet) and the Dweller in heaven (blue) (fig. 15).

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: All the pillars of the wall are of bronze, and their bases fixed in the ground are also of bronze, while the rods that join them are of silver and are fixed in hooks of silver. The meaning of this is that Christ is the wall of our salvation, who endured all sufferings for us, that is, the bronze, and He is the word of God, that is, the silver. Every spiritual person ought to be firm in the word of God and endure sufferings for His sake (fig. 15).

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: The dimensions of the wall are 100 cubits in length and 50 cubits in width, while the height is five cubits. It is understood from this that the linen pieces from which the wall is made are each 5 cubits x 5 cubits, and each piece is fixed on two pillars.

entries.section: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

paragraphs.text: It is noted that the vessels of the bronze altar, which people see, and likewise the pillars of the wall and its bases, are of bronze, so that whoever sees them may learn patience and endurance in the spiritual life.

Take care to guard your life with walls, which are the word of God in the Holy Bible, the guidance of your father of confession, your attachment to the means of grace, and partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord. In this way Christ will be a wall around your life and will keep it.

entries.section: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

paragraphs.text: The head of the family was its priest in the age of the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Then Moses performed the priestly work, and after that God chose Aaron and his sons to be priests to Him and asked Moses to do this, and they signify Christ the Great High Priest. The whole tribe of Levi helped the priests, the tribe that God set apart for His service, although Levi himself had sinned by killing the tribe of Shechem (Gen 34:25-30), but the mercy of God granted his descendants to be servants. The priests and Levites offered the sacrifices and offerings in the house of the Lord and took care of all the rites of worship in it and of its cleanliness and of moving it from place to place as God guided them, in addition to teaching the people the commandments of God and His worship, and examining sinners such as lepers, and they would decide their cleanness when God healed them.

entries.section: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

paragraphs.text: He asked Moses to make garments of a particular form for the priests, suited to the great service that they would perform before God, so that the garments they wear during the service would be worthy of the glory and splendor of God.

A person's appearance helps him toward the life he wants. Just as the priests' garments are fitting for being before God, so the clothes of the children of God should be fitting for them and show before people that they are children of God. So take care in your appearance, lest you cause anyone to stumble.

entries.section: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

paragraphs.text: Moses gathers the skilled craftsmen to make these garments, which proclaim that Aaron and his sons are consecrated, that is, set apart and dedicated to the service of God.

entries.section: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

paragraphs.text: Wise hearted: those skilled in the various crafts.

He mentions the details of the priest's garments, which are the "breastplate," which is placed on the ephod, which is the outer garment, and under it the robe, and then the broidered coat, in addition to the mitre and the girdle, all of which will be detailed in this chapter (fig. 16). The high priest wore these garments during his ordinary service every day, but on the Day of Atonement he humbled himself and wore only garments of linen in order to enter the Holy of Holies in them (Lev 16:4).

entries.section: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

paragraphs.text: These garments are made from materials that Moses collects from the people, and these materials have already been referred to and their meanings explained, and they are "gold, blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen (linen)."

The ephod is the outer garment; it is short and reaches the knees. It is made of linen, which signifies purity, blue, which signifies the heavenly life, purple, which signifies kingship, scarlet, which signifies the blood of Christ, and gold, which signifies God. The priest ought to be characterized by all this.

The ephod is made of two pieces joined together at the shoulders, and between them is an opening for the head, wider at the front than at the back, and the ephod is tied with a girdle, that is, a belt. That is, the ephod has no sleeves, like a vest.

A girdle or belt is made from the same cloth as the ephod; it is a belt tied around the waist to gather the ephod and all the priestly garments, and its two ends hang down from the waist in front toward the feet. This girdle signifies readiness and earnestness in work and spiritual striving, as any worker braces himself and ties up his waist so that his loose garments do not hinder him.
According to their birth: in the order of their birth, that is, the eldest and then the one younger than he.

God commanded Moses to bring two onyx stones, a kind of precious stone, and to engrave on each stone six names of the tribes of the children of Israel according to age, as an engraver engraves a signet, and to make for each stone a setting of gold around it, and they are fixed on the shoulders of Aaron to proclaim his responsibility for all the people, since he bears them on his shoulders, prays for them and cares for them, just as Christ carried the wood of the Cross on His shoulder for us, and He is our Great High Priest. His entering the Holy of Holies is an entering of all the people, carried on his shoulders, into the presence of God.
May you feel your responsibility for those around you, so that you pray for them, take care to draw them to the Church, show them your love and solve their problems.
Two chains of gold, plaited, are made, hanging from the two gold settings surrounding the two onyx stones.

The breastplate is the most important part of the high priest's garments, because in it are the Urim and the Thummim (v. 30), which reveal God's commands to His people. Therefore this breastplate was called the breastplate of judgment, because it proclaims God's judgment to His people.
The breastplate is made of the same cloth and materials as the ephod, which are gold, blue, purple, scarlet and fine twined linen (linen), and their meanings have been mentioned before (fig. 17).
Span = 20 cm.

It is made from a piece of cloth two spans long and a span wide, which is then folded, so that its length becomes a span and its width a span, and it is like a bag of cloth with its opening at the top.

Twelve precious stones are set on the breastplate in four rows, each containing three stones, and each stone is surrounded by a gold setting by which it is fixed on the breastplate. These precious stones are:
1- Red carnelian.
2- Yellow sapphire.
3- Emerald: a stone of a dark red color which, in the rays of the sun, appears like a flame of fire.
4- Ruby: its color is yellow inclining to red.
5- Blue sapphire.
6- White carnelian: a precious kind of carnelian.
7- Cat's eye: a transparent stone with black spots, so it resembles the eye of a cat.
8- Jade: a transparent stone with wavy lines.
9- Amethyst: its color is purple, that is, red inclining to violet.
10- Beryl: a transparent or green stone.
11- Onyx: a stone with parallel lines.
12- Jasper: a kind of precious crystal.

The name of a tribe is written on each stone, and by this God proclaims that Aaron enters before God with all the tribes, for Aaron is responsible for caring for them and prays for them. Aaron enters with the blood of animals and with the twelve tribes on his breast, and in this he signifies Christ, who offers His blood as redemption for all who believe in Him. Two things appear here:

1- The high priest bears the names of the tribes of the children of Israel on his breast, that is, beside his heart, so he feels all their problems and needs, which he carries on his shoulders through the two stones on which their names are engraved.
2- He feels for each individual of his people, for every tribe, indeed every individual, is a jewel in the eyes of the shepherd.

Two rings are made at the two ends of the breastplate at its top and sewn to it, and these two rings are tied by two braids of gold to the two settings in which the onyx stones are fixed, each inscribed with 6 names of the tribes and placed on Aaron's shoulder. Thus the breastplate is hung and suspended from above, that is, on the priest's breast, and tied to his shoulder, and around the breastplate on its four sides are twisted gold chains, so that they are like a cordon for it.

Two rings of gold are made and sewn to the lower end of the breastplate, and opposite them two other rings of gold are fixed in the ephod itself above the girdle, and the two lower rings of the breastplate are tied to the two rings above the girdle with a blue thread. Thus the breastplate is fixed at the top by the two gold chains and at the bottom by cloth threads of a blue color.

The breastplate is fixed on the ephod and bears the names of the twelve tribes, that is, when he enters the Holy Place or the Holy of Holies all the tribes enter with him. It is called the breastplate of judgment because by it God's judgment in the various affairs of the people is known. There are many opinions about how God's mind was proclaimed, among them that one or all of the stones inscribed with the names of the children of Israel fixed on the breastplate would light up (fig. 17). Figure (17:) The breastplate
The Urim: the lights.
The Thummim: the perfections.

The Urim and the Thummim are two stones placed inside the bag of the breastplate, and they are used to know God's judgment in the affairs of the people when the high priest enters the Holy Place for God to declare His will, and this is by means of:
1- These stones lighting up or not lighting up.
2- There is an opinion that on one of them was written "yes" and on the other "no," and God lights up one of them, and so the will of God is known.
May you ask God in all your needs to know His will, so that you submit to Him and not to your personal desires, and He will answer you and declare His mind if you are submissive to Him.
The robe is the garment worn under the ephod; it is longer than it and reaches below the knee, near the feet, and it is made of cloth of a blue color, that is, blue.

The robe is made in one piece, with the opening at its top for the head to go through, and a binding, that is, a band of cloth, is sewn on this opening to strengthen it so that it does not tear when the robe is put on or taken off, as coats of mail are strengthened, which are strong garments that warriors wear to protect them from arrows.

Small balls like a pomegranate are made of cloth or threads, some of them blue, some purple and others scarlet. Small bells are made, and a ball is hung, then a bell, that is, a little bell, and after that a ball and after it a bell, and so on, so that when the high priest enters the Holy of Holies the priests who are in the Holy Place do not see him but hear the sound of the bells. If he died inside the Holy of Holies, they would not hear the sound of the bells, and then they would draw him out by the rope tied to his foot into the Holy Place, because it is forbidden for anyone to enter the Holy of Holies except the high priest. In addition, the bells alert him to be exact in the worship of God and His service and in carrying out His commandments, lest He be angry with him and he die.

The pomegranates signify the fruits of the spiritual life that the priest and the people live, in addition to the fact that the seeds of the pomegranate are surrounded by a sweet red juice that signifies the blood of Christ, which cleanses us and adorns us with virtues. As for the little bells, that is, the bells, they signify:
1- The importance of the word of God, which the priest teaches to the people.
2- The awe of the priesthood.
3- The priest's attentiveness and exactness in his service.

May you be attentive when you stand to pray or when you read the Holy Bible, for you are in the presence of God, surrounded by His angels. As you feel the fear of Him, He opens your mind to understand His words and to enjoy His presence.
Engraving of a signet: that is, as is engraved on a signet.

He makes a plate of gold and engraves on it the words "Holiness to the Lord," to place it on the mitre of the high priest. It was called a crown in (ch. 29:6) because it is placed above the forehead of the high priest.

The gold plate is fixed on the mitre above the forehead with blue threads, that is, blue threads, to proclaim that the priest is consecrated to God, so he lives in purity and does nothing but the service of God. The blue threads proclaim that he is heavenly and lives the heavenly life.

The mitre with its gold plate proclaims the purity of the priest and his consecration to God, so when God sees his purity He forgives the people their shortcomings in their offerings and gifts to God. This is what is meant by "the iniquity of the holy things," for the priest completes the deficiencies of his people's worship by his prayers on their behalf.

May you care for those around you who are far from God, so that you pray for them, fast, prostrate yourself and ask God's help for them. As God sees your striving and your intercession for them, He will support you and them.
The garments of the priests, who are the sons of Aaron, consist of the following:
1- A coat like the high priest's, as mentioned before.

2- A bonnet, which is a head covering made of linen, resembling a fez or a large high cap, and it may have a veil, that is, a piece of cloth hanging down at the back attached to the bonnet, like the garments of the present-day priests.

3- A girdle, which is a piece of embroidered linen cloth tied around the waist with its end hanging down in front. All the priests' garments are of linen, a symbol of the purity and splendor that befit being in the presence of the great and glorified God.

The details of the ordination of the priests are mentioned here, which will be mentioned in the next chapter: he clothes them in their garments, anoints them with oil and consecrates them, that is, gives them sacrifices to offer before God.

He makes undergarments for the priests, which he calls breeches, from the waist to above the knee, and they signify modesty and the fear of God when entering the tent of meeting for the service and the offering of sacrifices, because if they neglect to wear these garments they sin against God and die in their iniquity.
These garments were for the service in the tent of meeting, but outside it they would wear their own garments as they wished.
In the Church of the New Testament the priests wear adorned white garments when they enter the sanctuary, for the following reasons:
1- They befit the greatness of God in His sanctuary, so they wear garments of splendor.
2- They call them and their people to purity when drawing near to God.
3- As a continuation of God's commands in the Old Testament concerning the priests' garments, because all stand before God.
4- In eternity they wear white garments (Rev 4:4, 6:11, 7:9, 15).

Your fear of God appears in your modesty when appearing before Him, so do not be preoccupied with appearance and clothes so that others may see you in them, but be as befits His presence. And when your relationship with Him grows, you will be modest at all times because He sees you.
The consecration of the priests: this chapter shows the steps of the ordination of the priests, which are:
1- Washing with water as a sign of purity of heart (v. 4).
2- Putting on the priestly garments, proclaiming the beginning of the new service filled with glory and splendor (vv. 5-9).
3- Anointing with holy oil as evidence of their consecration and their being set apart for the service of God (v. 7).
4- Offering a sin offering to make atonement for their sins (vv. 10-14).
5- Offering a burnt offering to be a sweet savour before the Lord (vv. 15-18).
6- Offering the ram of consecration as a peace offering, and waving parts of the sacrifice with the vegetable offering for their installation and their beginning the priestly service (vv. 19-25).
7- Eating of the sacrifice as a sign of their fellowship with God and a reward for their blessed work (vv. 26, 27).
Without blemish: without defect.
It specifies the requirements for the day of the ordination of the priests and their consecration to the priestly work, which God commanded Moses to prepare, and they are:
1- The bullock: offered as a sin offering.
2- A ram as a burnt offering.
3- Another ram as an offering of consecration.
These sacrifices signify Christ, who offers Himself for us on the Cross and sheds His blood for us, and by His blood gives the Church her Holy Sacraments, among them the sacrament of the priesthood.

Besides the sacrifices, Moses prepares a vegetable offering consisting of doughs made of the finest kind of flour, which is wheat, and they signify the life of Christ on earth, which is without blemish. The offering includes three kinds:-
1- Unleavened bread, that is, without leaven, because leaven signifies the evil that spreads inside a person, as Christ spoke of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is their hypocrisy (Lk 12:1).
2- Cakes unleavened, tempered with oil, that is, kneaded with oil. We note here the addition of oil, which signifies the work of the Holy Spirit.
3- Wafers unleavened anointed with oil, which are like the previous cakes but thinner than they.
In the three previous kinds the variety is to be noted, and what is meant by it is the variety of virtues in the life of Christ and in the life of the priest consecrated to God.

The kinds of bread mentioned above are put in one basket, because they signify the life of the one Christ who redeems all humanity and the priest who prays for all his people. The sacrifices and the basket are offered before God on the day of the ordination of the priests.

Take care to prepare everything that the service needs so that it may be complete before God, and take more care to prepare yourself for prayer by driving away every evil thought and remembering the greatness of being before God. Reading the Holy Bible, examining yourself or repeating a hymn ... etc. helps you in this. This makes you feel the presence of God and enjoy the depth of the words of prayer.

entries.section: (2) The steps of consecrating the priests

paragraphs.text: The first step in consecrating the priests is washing them with water, that is, a complete bath, and this was in the laver set up inside the tent of meeting before entering the Holy Place. It signifies purity from every sin and the rejection of evil. This rite is still performed in the Divine Liturgy by the priest washing his hands before beginning it.

entries.section: (2) The steps of consecrating the priests

paragraphs.text: The second step is putting on the priestly garments. He first puts on the coat and ties it with a girdle at the waist, then puts on the robe, and after that puts the ephod over it and ties it with the girdle at the waist, and puts the breastplate on his breast, in which are the Urim and the Thummim, then puts on the mitre, and on it the crown, that is, the gold plate on which is written Holiness to the Lord. These garments that the high priest wears signify putting on righteousness and a good life with God, and his bearing the responsibility of caring for his people, who are on his breast and on his shoulder, as we mentioned in

entries.section: (2) The steps of consecrating the priests

paragraphs.text: The third step is anointing with oil, which is a mixture of sweet-smelling materials blended with oil, as will be mentioned in (ch. 30), and it is also called the oil of gladness (Ps 45:7) and "the precious ointment" (Ps 133:2). The anointing is done by pouring the oil on the head of Aaron, in addition to anointing him and his garments with oil. The oil signifies the Holy Spirit, who descends on the priest and works in him and gives him the power to carry out the service of the priesthood, and which became a sacrament of the Church in the New Testament. The anointing with sweet oil also signifies:
1- That the priests are the sweet fragrance to God before and in the midst of their people.
2- Just as oil is used for lighting, the priests give light and are a light in the midst of their people.
3- The anointing of the priests in the Old Testament signifies Christ, who was anointed with the Holy Spirit to accomplish our redemption (Lk 4:

entries.section: (2) The steps of consecrating the priests

paragraphs.text: "Gird bonnets on them": that is, put bonnets on them.

As for the priests, Moses clothes them in their priestly garments, which are fewer than the garments of Aaron the high priest. They put on coats and tie them with a girdle at the waist, then bonnets on their heads, which were most probably a cap around which a piece of cloth is wound, like the winding of a turban among some people. They are anointed with oil, but oil is not poured on their heads, for this distinguishes the high priest to proclaim that he is the head of the priesthood.

"Consecrating them" means their being filled with the grace of God to exercise the priesthood, and also they take of the sacrifice of consecration and eat of it, and this signifies the spiritual satisfaction that the priest receives, for he is satisfied spiritually and materially and lacks nothing.

Filling the hand also means sharing in offering the sacrifice by carrying a part of it and moving it before God, that is, beginning the priestly service. That is, filling the hand is the sanctification of the priests, that is, setting them apart for the priestly service and their beginning in it.

The service of God is very great, so if you approach it in any work, even a small one, take care to repent of every sin and to adorn yourself with the virtues that the Holy Spirit helps you to acquire, and you will be able to experience the work of God in the service and rejoice in it.

The consecration, that is, the ordination of these priests, is done by the hand of Moses, who signifies the bishop or the Patriarch, before the tent of meeting, which signifies the Church, that is, they are ordained before God and before His people. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the bullock so that their sins are transferred from their heads. It is a symbol of the sacrament of confession, where the sin is transferred from the head of the penitent to Christ, who was slain for us on the Cross.

This bullock is a sin offering and it signifies the sacrifice of the Cross in one of its aspects, and it bears the sins of men, among them the priests, because he too is a man liable to fall into sin, so it is slain before the tent of meeting, proclaiming that salvation is in the Church.

The blood is gathered in basins as before, which are called pans, that is, flat vessels (ch. 27:3), and Moses takes some of it and puts it on the horns of the altar, which signify strength, that is, the sacrifice of Christ is strong and offers complete forgiveness to whoever believes in Him, confesses his sins and approaches the sacrament of the priesthood.

The rest of the blood he pours at the bottom of the altar, and perhaps what is meant is that the blood falls into the compass, which is like a concave shelf at the middle of the altar, so that the blood does not fall on the ground (ch. 27:5). The anointing of the altar with blood is done to sanctify it because of the sins of the people that defile it and anger God (v. 36, Lev 8:15, 16:16). And because the life of the animal is in its blood, pouring it at the bottom of the altar is a declaration by man that the blood of the animal makes atonement for him instead of the death of man himself, and this signifies the blood of Christ, who died for us and redeemed us.

The fat is the richest thing inside the body of the animal, so it is always offered to God and burned on the altar, with part of the liver and the two kidneys because of their importance as well. It is understood from this that the animal is cut open and its inside exposed, and this signifies a person's examining his thoughts and the intentions of his heart and everything inside him.

May you examine yourself every day before God and offer repentance for all your sins, even if they are in thought or intention, so that you are purified and the words of prayer and praise take their place, and you become a sacrifice of love before Him, like the fat that is burned on the altar.
His dung: the waste of the bullock that is inside its digestive system.

The rest of the animal, that is, its flesh, its skin and its dung, is burned outside the camp, that is, the place where the children of Israel dwell, as a symbol of God's aversion to sin. This bullock is a sin offering, so it is burned far from God, who hates sin. The sin offering signifies Christ, who bore our sins and died for us on the Cross outside the camp, that is, outside Jerusalem.

Moses takes one of the two rams, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head, proclaiming that this ram will stand in their place before God. It signifies Christ, who was offered for us on the Cross and pleased God by His pure life, so God is pleased with us if we believe in Him and live with Him.

The ram is slain to be offered as a burnt offering before God, as a symbol of Christ, who is without sin and died for us, that the Father might smell a sweet savour on our behalf, and the blood of the ram is sprinkled on the four sides of the bronze altar, so it flows and gathers in the compass, that is, the shelf below the surface of the altar.

He takes care to cut the ram into pieces, as a symbol of the sufferings of Christ that He passed through throughout His life, and these pieces and all its inside are washed, proclaiming its purity outwardly and inwardly, for it signifies the righteous Christ, who died for us to be a sweet savour before God. This points to the importance of the priest's purity inwardly and outwardly, that is, in his conduct and his thoughts.

Accept pain and weariness for the sake of God, and endure insults and false accusations with purity of heart and without agitation, and you will become a sacrifice of love and a sweet savour before God.
The flesh of the animal and everything in it is burned on the altar as a burnt offering to please God.

The second ram is offered as an offering of consecration, that is, a sacrifice from which they fill their hands and with which they begin to practice the sacrament of the priesthood (Lev 8:22), and they take of it to eat, to proclaim a fellowship of love between them and God. Therefore Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the sacrifice to proclaim their love for God, and He in His love gives them of it to eat, so that they share with Him in one feeling of love.

After the ram is slain, Moses takes some of the blood and touches the tip of the ear of Aaron and of his sons, which is the soft lower part of the flesh of the ear, and it signifies the sanctification of the ear to hear the word of God. He also touches the thumb of the right hand, which is the most important finger of the hand, as a symbol of the sanctification of the works of the priests and their consecration to God. Then he touches the great toe of the right foot, which is the most important toe of the foot, as a symbol of the sanctification of their conduct and all their ways to God. The right members were chosen because they signify strength and blessing, and these members represent the whole man. The blood is sprinkled on the four sides of the altar, like the rite of the burnt offering.

After that he sprinkles some of the blood on the priests and their garments, as a symbol that their priesthood is taken from the blood of Christ, then he sprinkles some of the anointing oil, which proclaims their consecration to the service of the Lord. The blood signifies the covenant between God and the priests, and the anointing with oil signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit given to them to perform their service.
The rump: the tail of the sheep, full of fat.

The offering of consecration is a kind of peace offering in which the one who offers it shares in eating of it, and the offering of consecration is offered only on the day of the priest's ordination, because it is a proclamation of the beginning of his service and its being handed over to him. In this sacrifice Moses takes all the fat that is in the sacrifice with part of the liver and the two kidneys and offers it on the altar to God to be burned, as is the custom in all the sacrifices, because God first takes the richest and most important part of the sacrifice, and to it is added the right shoulder of the ram, which is what the priest takes from the sacrifices of the people. Here, however, because the sacrifice is offered on behalf of the priest, God takes the right shoulder to be burned on the altar, and it signifies works, for the right hand signifies strength, so strong works are offered to God before man uses his strength for his own needs.

To what is offered to God of the offering of consecration is added a sample of each of the material offerings, because when God takes of the offering He blesses the rest of the food when the priests eat it.

Be careful to offer to God the firstfruits of your time and your abilities, to proclaim your love for Him, and He will bless the rest of your works and thoughts, and you will always enjoy His fellowship.

Moses places the fat, the right shoulder and the material offerings on the hands of Aaron and his sons, to proclaim that they are the ones who offer them before the Lord with pleasure and joy. Waving means a horizontal movement of the hand forward, then backward, then right and after that left, so they offer the offering to God, who is glorified in the four directions of the world. They offer it forward toward the altar, that is, God, then backward, that is, toward themselves, and so they receive a blessing by offering this sacrifice, then they move their hands right and left, that is, the whole people whom they shepherd receive a blessing from their priestly service.

All these parts of the ram of consecration, with the vegetable offerings, that is, the unleavened bread, the tempered cakes and the wafers, are offered to God as a sacrifice of love, and Moses burns them on the altar.
The ram of consecration, which is Aaron's: that is, the ram offered for the consecration of Aaron and his sons.
The breast: the bone to which the chest of the sacrifice is attached, containing the greatest amount of flesh and the finest.

The breast, or chest of the sacrifice, Moses carries on his hands and waves, that is, lifts up, because it is offered to God who dwells in heaven, and brings it down, that is, it is given as a gift from God to him, then he takes it to cook it and eat it, he and his household. This is a proclamation of the blessing that the priest receives from his service, which he takes here in material form as a part of the sacrifice, and it also signifies the spiritual blessings that the priest of the New Testament receives from his service.
Heave offering: the sacrifice or offering that is lifted up to God who dwells in heaven, that is, offered to Him.

God declares here to Moses that the priest's portion of the sacrifices that the people offer is the breast, or chest, of the sacrifice and the right shoulder, and he takes them as food for himself and his household from the peace offerings. As for this sacrifice offered on the day of Aaron's ordination, Moses took the breast, but throughout their days the priest takes the breast from the sacrifices of the people.

Take care to offer your love to God, whether in holy worship or in service to Him, for it is a blessing to you, in addition to its gladdening the heart of God, who pours out His mercies on you, setting before your eyes His love that He offered to you on the Cross, that you may respond to it with what you offer to Him.

The priestly garments that were sanctified by the anointing of Aaron the high priest are worn by the one who is appointed high priest after his death, in order to sanctify these great garments because they entered before God and His service.

How great it is to enter before God, and greater than it is to partake of His Holy Mysteries. So take care for the day of your partaking of the Holy Mysteries and enjoy entering the Church, that is, into the presence of God. Indeed, it is also possible for you to enjoy it whether in your chamber or in any place, so that not only your garments but your heart also becomes holy.

The rite of consecrating the priests or the high priest is that he remain in these garments seven days inside the tent of meeting, to enjoy the presence of God and be filled with His grace at the beginning of his service, as is mentioned in detail in (Lev 8:33-35). In the New Testament the new priest enjoys a retreat of 40 days in the monastery.

entries.section: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

paragraphs.text: After the fat and the right shoulder are burned on the altar and Moses takes the breast or chest, the priests take the rest of the flesh of the ram and cook it beside the door of the tent of meeting, that is, they do not leave the tent of meeting.

entries.section: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

paragraphs.text: Those with which the atonement was made: that is, Aaron and his sons, for whom it was offered.
A stranger: one who is not of the priests.

Aaron and his sons, that is, all the priests, eat of the flesh of the ram because it is an atoning sacrifice for them, and this is at the door of the tent of meeting because they are guests of God, so they are sanctified and consecrated to the service of God. This eating means making a covenant with God that they be consecrated to His service, and He is responsible for them and provides for their spiritual and material needs, in addition to the priests' doing all their works before God, that is, pleasing Him. This is a symbol of the atoning sacrifice of Christ for His priests in the sacrament of the priesthood and its power given in this sacrament.

entries.section: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

paragraphs.text: The offering of consecration, like the peace offering, is eaten of by the one who offers it, and it signifies the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord. Out of sanctification of it nothing of it remains to the next day, and if any remains it is burned, because if anything of the offering of consecration remained it would be liable to corruption or someone other than the priests might eat of it and sin. It is not eaten on the next day because it is holy, that is, set apart for the priests, so they eat it on the day of their consecration.
The ram of consecration also signifies Christ, who was slain on the Cross to consecrate priests for the service of His people and that they may be stewards of His mysteries.

entries.section: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

paragraphs.text: What was done on the first day for the consecration of the priests is repeated, which is offering a bullock and two rams for seven days, and these offerings are offered daily. This is to confirm the holiness of the priesthood and so that the priest may remain inside the tent of meeting, as the priest of the New Testament remains 40 days in the monastery after his ordination.

entries.section: (7) The food of the priests and the consecration of the altar

paragraphs.text: Most holy: the bronze altar becomes holy, equal to the Holy of Holies.

These sacrifices, that is, the bullock and the two rams, which are offered daily, sanctify and consecrate not only the priests but the bronze altar also, so the altar becomes holy and sanctifies and blesses whoever touches it.

The sacrament of Holy Communion sanctifies your life and consecrates your heart to God, so be careful to practice it throughout the year and before great undertakings, that He may bless you in your life.
Of the first year: that is, a year old, a reference to complete growth and maturity and at the same time to innocence and purity.

After the ordination of the priests, God spoke to them about the daily burnt offerings that the priests would offer to Him immediately after their ordination, which are two lambs of the first year, one a morning burnt offering and the other an evening burnt offering. On the bronze altar a lamb one year old is offered in the morning as a burnt offering to please God, and before its fire goes out, between the two evenings, that is, between three and five in the afternoon, another burnt offering is offered, so that a fire always remains burning on the altar. This fire came down from heaven the first time and then remained burning on the altar throughout the years by these burnt offerings, besides the various burnt offerings of the people.
A tenth deal: that is, a tenth of an ephah, and the ephah equals 23 liters, so its tenth equals 2.3 liters.
The hin: equals 3.8 liters, and its fourth part equals about a liter.
Beaten oil: olive oil pressed by beating, not by crushing, and the former is purer.

With the morning or evening burnt offering is offered a tenth of an ephah of flour kneaded with a fourth part of a hin of oil. The flour and the oil represent the fruits of the earth, and of them is offered to God that He may afterward bless the food of His people. The flour also signifies the holy offering, while the oil signifies the Holy Spirit.
A fourth part of a hin of wine is also poured on the sacrifice. Wine too is of the fruits of the earth, that God may bless the harvest of the grapes and the wine of His people.
In the New Testament the wine is changed into the Blood of Christ, so the pouring out of wine signifies the sacrifice of the New Testament.

How beautiful it is to offer to God of your money and possessions for the Church and the needy, for God blesses all that you have until it is more than you need and you feel rest and peace in your heart.
An evening burnt offering is also offered, like the morning one, gladdening the heart of God, for it shows His people's love for Him in their holy worship.
At the door of the tent of meeting: that is, on the bronze altar that is in front of the door of the tent.

The offering of these burnt offerings continues throughout life on the bronze altar near the door of the tent of meeting, and there God speaks with Moses and his allies of the priests and prophets and makes clear to His people how they are to live with Him. These sacrifices continued to be offered throughout the Old Testament as evidence of the insufficiency of the sacrifice to satisfy God, for it was merely a symbol of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, which He offered once and which atoned for all humanity who believe in Him.
When God appears in the form of a cloud before the tent of meeting, He blesses His people and sanctifies them and cleanses them.
God promises to sanctify the tent of meeting and the priests if they offer the previous sacrifices in this chapter.
How beautiful are the feelings of God, who wishes to restore the life of the first Paradise, so that as He was with Adam and Eve He may be with His people and in their midst to bless them always.
When the people see God dwelling in the cloud before them, they feel His greatness and His power which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they remain firm in faith in Him.
The altar of incense, the laver, the composition of the oil and incense, and the silver of the ransom

The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place, before the Holy of Holies. It is different from the bronze altar, which stands before the door of the tabernacle of meeting in the outer court. It is made of durable acacia wood that does not rot and is overlaid with plates of gold (v. 38). As we said concerning the Ark of the Covenant, the wood signifies the humanity of Christ and the gold His divinity; the wood also signifies the Virgin, while the gold signifies Christ who was born of her womb (Figure 18). Figure (18:) The altar of incense

The dimensions of the altar of incense are a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, that is, square, and its height is two cubits. It has four horns, which are part of the corner post and not horns attached to it, to declare that the altar's strength comes from itself. It signifies the mighty Christ, who offered Himself up on the Cross as an atoning sacrifice for us, like the fragrance of incense with which God is pleased with man.

The top of the altar, all its sides and its horns are covered with gold, that is, the divinity was united with the humanity perfectly in Christ. A crown, that is, a raised border, is made for it around its upper surface, as a beautiful sight and to protect the incense and the coals from falling to the ground.

Two gold rings are made, joined and united to the altar on its two sides, so that a pole of acacia wood overlaid with gold may be put through each of them to carry it. The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place before the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies; on its right is the table of showbread and on its left the golden lampstand.
Aaron: all the priests are meant.
He dresses the lamps: he prepares them and makes them ready.
He lights the lamps: that is, he kindles them.

The priests place the incense every morning and every evening when they change the oil and replenish it in the lampstand so that it gives light morning and evening. In the same way, they offer a burnt offering on the bronze altar morning and evening. All these declare that Christ offers for us a complete and continual redemption that rises as a sweet fragrance before God, so that He is pleased with us. He is the light of the world, and He works always in the believers by His Holy Spirit, like the continual incense and the lampstand that shines always in the Holy Place.
He warns against three things concerning the altar of incense, which are:

1- Offering strange incense other than the composition that God told Moses about, which will be mentioned in this same chapter (v. 34). This is a declaration that Christ alone, whom the incense signifies, is the Redeemer.
2- No sacrifice or offering is to be offered on it, because these are offered on the bronze altar, whereas this altar is set apart for incense only.
3- No wine or oil is to be poured on it, as is done on the bronze altar.

For the same purpose, namely that this altar is set apart for incense, the rite here declares one aspect of the Cross, which is the incense that signifies Christ, who pleased the Father by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross like the fragrance of incense.
Most holy to the Lord: it is set apart for the service of God and cannot be used for any other purpose.

Aaron puts the blood on it once every year on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:18, 19) before he enters the Holy of Holies with the incense. This confirms that the incense is a symbol of Christ who was slain for us on the Cross. The blood is an atonement for the sins of the priest and the people, and so the blood is mingled with the incense on the altar of incense, because the two are symbols of the one sacrifice of Christ.

May you be like Christ, so that you are a sweet fragrance before God through your thoughts, your words and your deeds. Rather, be distinct from the rest of the world, as a child of God who has the fragrance of Christ, and do not resemble the people of the world in their faults.

God commanded that the people be numbered and that a ransom be paid for each one of the males. Every man twenty years old and above pays an amount of silver to redeem his soul, and this is for the following reasons:
1- A declaration of every person's need of the redemption of Christ, who is the Word of God and is signified by the silver.

2- Thanksgiving to God, who redeemed the firstborn of the children of Israel, and the destroying angel did not kill them in Egypt. This signifies responding to the love of Christ the Redeemer, who gave Himself on the Cross for His children, so we give Him our money, that is, the silver.

God warned against neglecting the numbering and the payment of the ransom, lest a plague come upon them as happened in the days of David. God's anger against David was because of his numbering of the people, for:
1- God had not commanded him to make this numbering.
2- David tried to boast of their number, that is, he fell into the sin of pride (2 Sam 24:10-17).

Twenty years old: the completion of maturity and the age of majority. Whoever reaches this age joins the army to fight (Num 1:3). The tribe of Levi was exempted from paying the ransom because they are consecrated to the service of the Lord (Num 1:

47-53.(Everyone who passes over to those who are numbered: that is, everyone who has reached the age of twenty and above and has passed under the counting. The shekel of the sanctuary: the priests kept accurate scales in the Temple, so it was called the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, a shekel that is exact and precise, more than the ordinary shekel, and it is about 12 grams of silver.
Gerah: that is, a grain, because it weighs a carob seed, and it equals 1/20 of the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, about 0.6 grams.

Every man offered half a shekel, that is, about 6 grams (some say 8 or 9 grams), which in any case is an amount of silver that both the poor and the rich can pay, since every soul has the same value before God, whether the person is rich or poor. It is a symbol of man's response to God's love and his appreciation of redemption. Christ paid the tax of the two drachmas, which is the ransom (Mt 17:24-27).

This silver is used in the building materials of the tabernacle of meeting, that is, for the bases of the pillars and the hooks. The silver signifies Christ the Redeemer, for redemption is the foundation of the spiritual building.

Remember the love of Christ the Redeemer and His care for you, so that you may respond to it, not only by giving the firstfruits and the tithes, but by serving God and laying down your life for His sake.

The laver is a wide vessel, most likely circular in shape, with a base on which it rests. It is made of bronze, which signifies steadfastness and strength, and water is put in it, and it is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place. It signifies Baptism, by which we are born again and are established in the life with God. It is circular because it signifies the salvation offered to the whole world, and no measurements were specified for it, so that it might declare salvation to everyone who believes in Christ (Figure 19). Figure (19:) The laver

The priests wash in this laver before they come forward to serve, as a declaration of the importance of purity before entering the service of God, and as a symbol of Baptism, the entrance to the spiritual life. The laver is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place, but washing in it is required before entering any service, whether at the bronze altar or in the Holy Place. It was placed before the Holy Place because those who wash in it are the priests only, who alone enter the Holy Place.
The washing of the hands is a sign of the purity of deeds, and the washing of the feet a sign of the purity of conduct.

Washing was necessary, otherwise the priest would die if he entered without washing, since this would be considered contempt for God's commands and His dwelling place. Washing is a symbol of the purity that Christ the Redeemer gives us.

Take care of the purity of your mind and its cleansing, and of casting all your troubles on God, before any spiritual work such as prayer at home, the Divine Liturgy, or reading the Holy Bible, by reading a psalm, making prostrations (metanoias), or repeating a hymn....
Calamus: a sweet fragrance.
Spices of fragrance: that is, a perfumed or sweetened perfume.
1- Pure myrrh (liquid myrrh): a gum that flows from one of the thorny trees and falls from it in drops, so it is called liquid myrrh, and it is the purest kind of myrrh since it has no impurities.
2- Sweet cinnamon: the inner bark of the cinnamon tree, which has a well-known sweet fragrance in addition to its pleasant taste.
3- Sweet calamus: a kind of reed that has a sweet fragrance.

4- Cassia: the bark of one of the trees, which has a sweet fragrance. Some say it is the outer bark of the cinnamon tree, though it may be another tree. It is called cassia (salikha) because the outer bark is stripped (tuslakh) from the trees.

God specified the quantities of these materials to be mixed together, with a hin of olive oil added to them, which is about 4 liters. These quantities come in the end to about 18 kilograms. Thus the anointing oil is formed with a sweet fragrance, and with it the kings, priests and prophets are anointed. It signifies the Sacrament of the Holy Myron.

He commanded him to anoint all the parts of the tabernacle of meeting, so that they would be dedicated, or sanctified, or consecrated to God, and a blessing to everyone who touches them, and not be used for anything except worship.
This anointing is used to anoint the priests, as has passed in (ch. 29).

This oil differs from all the perfumed oils that people use to give a fragrance to their bodies, and even if they use the same materials, they would be in different quantities. But whoever disobeys the word of God and makes the same exactly, to perfume his own body or the body of any person who is a stranger to the children of Israel, that person is set apart and cut off, that is, he does not become a member in the congregation of God.

May you have the virtues that adorn your life, and likewise holy worship and self-sacrificing service, so that your fragrance may be sweet before God, like the anointing oil, which is the work of the Holy Spirit.
The Lord gave Moses the ingredients of the composition of the incense, which are:-
1- Stacte: the gum of the storax tree.
2- Onycha: the shells of a water creature called the "winged-shell mollusk," which has a sweet fragrance when burned.
3- Galbanum: one of the fragrant gums.
4- Frankincense: a gum from thorny trees.
All these materials are mixed in equal quantities, and they give a sweet fragrance when burned.
These materials are mixed with salt and become holy incense, that is, set apart for the worship of God.
The preceding materials are beaten small, and they become the holy incense, which is placed in a golden vessel beside the altar of incense, before the Holy of Holies.

This incense, with the preceding quantities, is set apart for the worship of God, and no one may make the like of it to enjoy its fragrance in his house, out of honor and sanctification of this incense. Whoever makes the like of it is cut off from the people of God, that is, he is cast out and loses his membership.
The Church in the New Testament uses incense for the following reasons:
1- It was and still is offered as honor to God. God commanded it to Moses in the Old Testament, and its idea remains firm in the New Testament.
2- Offering feelings of love for God, like the sinful woman in the house of Simon (Lk 7:36-50) and like David in his prayers (Ps 141:2).
3- It signifies Christ the Redeemer, who offered His life for us on the Cross, and His good Father smelled a sweet fragrance on Golgotha.
4- It signifies the prayers of the saints and of all the believers, with which God rejoices, as the Book of Revelation declares (Rev 5:8, 8:3, 4).
5- Just as incense rises toward heaven as a sweet fragrance, so the life of the believers should rise with their virtues as a sweet fragrance toward heaven.

For your fragrance to be sweet before God, your life must be mixed with many virtues, and you must crush yourself with the sorrows of toil and spiritual striving, so that your heart and your life become holy to Christ.
The makers of the tabernacle of meeting and the sanctification of the Sabbath

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: Bezaleel: his name means in the shadow or protection of God. He was the grandson of Hur, who supported the hand of Moses when he was praying at the time of the war with Amalek (ch. 17:10). Because of the greatness of the house of God, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, after He had specified to Moses everything in the tabernacle, its measurements and its design, He also supported it by choosing the one responsible for making the tabernacle. He chose a Jewish man named Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ, the leader of the journey of our salvation, came, and made him the chief of the craftsmen for the work of the house of God. The following is noted in his selection:
1- The most important arrangement for completing the service is the servant himself, so God took care in choosing Bezaleel to lead the work.

2- God chose him because he knew many crafts, which he had learned in Egypt, advanced in the arts at that time, and then filled him with understanding and knowledge by His Holy Spirit. Thus the grace of God is mingled with human knowledge, whose source is also God.

3- He knows many trades; he is an artist and is able to lead the craftsmen in the various crafts, even if some of them are more skilled than he in a particular craft, yet he is able to lead them. The leader organizes the work and leads it even if some of his followers are more gifted than he in a certain part of the work.

Care for the leader of every ministry and support him spiritually, emotionally and materially so that he may lead the work. Pray that God will send him, and be careful in your choice of him. And if you are a leader, take care for the purity of your heart and trust in God in everything, so that He may do His work.

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: Aholiab: the meaning of his name is tent of the father. God chose him from the tribe of Dan, which is the least of the tribes in standing, because God loves everyone and chooses His servants from every place. Just as He chose Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ came, He chose Aholiab from a tribe of lesser rank.

To complete the service, God commanded Moses to appoint a helper for Bezaleel, namely Aholiab, and likewise to call all the artists in the various crafts to take part in this great work, to confirm the importance of cooperation and participation in work within the Church.

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: He did not forget anything inside the tabernacle of meeting, whether the furniture or the materials used, for everything has value in the house of God and must be cared for because it is in the house of God.
At the end of God's talk with Moses on the mountain, He returns to confirm the importance of keeping the Sabbath. The following is noted in this commandment:
1- He calls them "My Sabbaths," for the people of God sanctify the seventh day for the sake of God, His worship and His love.

2- Keeping the day of God every week is a sign of our sonship to God. By this we differ from the rest of mankind, who do not care to set apart a day for God. It is like a covenant between God and His people throughout all the days.

3- He repeats it after the command to make the tabernacle of meeting, lest the workers think that it is permitted to work on erecting the tabernacle on the Sabbath days. It was required to devote oneself to worship only on this day.

If the glory of Sunday has surpassed the glory of the Sabbath because of the Resurrection of Christ, the Sabbath signifies rest not only in the completion of the creation of the world, but it signifies Sunday, on which Christ completed our redemption and proclaimed our salvation. Therefore may you take care to sanctify Sunday and give yourself a greater opportunity on it to enjoy the worship of God and His service, so that you experience His work in you more deeply.
Profanes it: breaks it.
God completes His commandments of the law of the Sabbath, saying:

4- The penalty for breaking the Sabbath by doing material works on it was severe, namely death, because the Sabbath signifies the devotion of the heart to God. Whoever lets the love of the world into his heart profanes it and has no life with Christ. This is the first time the penalty for breaking the Sabbath is mentioned, as it is mentioned in (Num 15:

God rested and was refreshed: what is meant is God's satisfaction with His work, for God does not grow weary or breathe as human beings do, but He speaks in expressions that human beings understand, to teach them that rest is a spiritual rest, by being with God.
God adds in the law of the Sabbath:

5- The necessity of holding fast to it throughout their lives and in all generations, that is, their children. Even now the Sabbath day has respect in the Church, but the glory of Sunday has surpassed it, so the Church celebrates Sunday and also the Sabbath of every week, and does not fast strictly on them nor make prostrations (metanoias), because they are days of joy. Here He stresses the importance of continuing to keep the Sabbath, that is, carrying out God's commandments throughout life.

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: Moses represented the image of God to the people. So when he went up the mountain and was absent there for days, they needed a tangible image, as they had seen images of gods in Egypt. They asked Aaron for a tangible image of God to worship in place of Moses, because they doubted whether he might have died on the mountain, since he had no food or drink for the whole forty days (ch. 25:18), or whether he had lost his way in the mountain, or the divine fire had burned him. Some of them may have thought that he had been caught up to heaven like Enoch. Moses spent another forty days fasting on the mountain (ch. 34:28) to receive two new tablets of the commandments, after he broke the first two tablets when he came down from the mountain and saw the golden calf (v. 19).

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: Fashioned it: melted it so that it became a single mass.

Aaron yielded to the people's sinful demands. This was weakness of faith and fear on his part before the people's uprising. So he collected from them the golden earrings that were in their ears, melted them in the fire, and fashioned them with a graving tool, and he formed a calf from this gold and called it the god who brought the children of Israel out of Egypt by the ten plagues. This was a belittling of God by depicting Him as a calf, as they used to worship the calf "Apis" in Egypt or watch the Egyptians worship it. Notice the generosity of the people in giving to make the golden calf, just as we give much of our time and effort to evil. Notice also that the Holy Bible mentions the sins of the saints just as it mentions their virtues, so that we are not troubled if we fall into sin, but rise and continue our spiritual striving with God.

Hold fast to the word of God as a servant, and do not yield to the demands of those you serve in order to please them against the commandments of God, so that your only aim in every service is to draw souls to Christ.

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: After Aaron set up the golden calf, raised before the people, he built an altar before it and offered sacrifices on it, and they ate of them. It appears that peace offerings, part of which is burned before God on the altar while the one who offers them eats the remainder, were known among the fathers since the days of Adam. By this Aaron proclaimed a feast to the Lord Jehovah, depicted in the form of this golden calf. By making the golden calf and what they did before it, they fell into these errors:
(1) Belittling God and depicting Him as a golden calf.
(2) Offering sacrifices to this idol, which neither hears nor sees nor walks.
(3) They were absorbed in eating meat, rather than in repentance joined with offering sacrifices to God.
(4) They took part in licentious and shameless games to please their lusts, and most likely these were joined with drinking wine.

At the end of the forty days, after God finished His talk with Moses, He informed him of the evil into which the people had fallen, and commanded him to go down from the mountain to the people, who had become corrupt by making a golden calf. They offered it worship and sacrifices, and even attributed to it the power of bringing them out of the land of Egypt, and they departed far from their God. In God's distress over the people, He called them "your people," for they were no longer the people of God, because they had exchanged Him for a golden calf.

Do not lose the grace of your sonship to God, in which you enjoy a relationship of love with Him and His care, and even the eternal inheritance. Do not give up all this for any earthly lust, however pleasant or dazzling it may seem, for it is passing away and is worth nothing beside your sonship to God.

Stiff-necked: like the ox that refuses to have the yoke placed on its neck, or the horse that resists with its neck the bridle placed in its mouth. What is meant is that the people of God are obstinate like these animals. God described His people as obstinate and as refusing life with Him, and He declared to Moses that He intended to destroy this people for their wickedness and to raise up a new people from his offspring, because he had found grace in His eyes, like Noah and Abraham. We notice Moses' boldness with God, so that he even asks His permission and He says to him, "Let Me alone." For God loves His children, and they have a great place with Him. He of course knows that Moses will intercede for the people and that He will not destroy them, but He declares how wicked they are and how much they deserve, without destroying them.
Repented of the evil: ceased from taking vengeance on them.
Moses raised his prayers in humility before God, pleading for His mercies, that He would forgive His people and not destroy them, for the following reasons:

1- Because they are the people of God, who kept them in Egypt and brought them out with great power and cares for them in the wilderness. They are His own and His children, and by this he seeks the tenderness and fatherhood of God.
